  "new_string": "\treturn nil\n}\n\n// UpdateCommitted replaces the transcript, prompts, and context for an existing\n// committed checkpoint. Uses replace semantics: the full session transcript is\n// written, replacing whatever was stored at initial condensation time.\n//\n// This is called at stop time to finalize all checkpoints from the current turn\n// with the complete session transcript (from prompt to stop event).\n//\n// Returns ErrCheckpointNotFound if the checkpoint doesn't exist.\nfunc (s *GitStore) UpdateCommitted(ctx context.Context, opts UpdateCommittedOptions) error {\n\tif opts.CheckpointID.IsEmpty() {\n\t\treturn errors.New(\"invalid update options: checkpoint ID is required\")\n\t}\n\n\t// Ensure sessions branch exists\n\tif err := s.ensureSessionsBranch(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to ensure sessions branch: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\n\t// Get current branch tip and flatten tree\n\tref, entries, err := s.getSessionsBranchEntries()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\t// Read root CheckpointSummary to find the session slot\n\tbasePath := opts.CheckpointID.Path() + \"/\"\n\trootMetadataPath := basePath + paths.MetadataFileName\n\tentry, exists := entries[rootMetadataPath]\n\tif !exists {\n\t\treturn ErrCheckpointNotFound\n\t}\n\n\tcheckpointSummary, err := s.readSummaryFromBlob(entry.Hash)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to read checkpoint summary: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif len(checkpointSummary.Sessions) == 0 {\n\t\treturn ErrCheckpointNotFound\n\t}\n\n\t// Find session index matching opts.SessionID\n\tsessionIndex := -1\n\tfor i := range len(checkpointSummary.Sessions) {\n\t\tmetaPath := fmt.Sprintf(\"%s%d/%s\", basePath, i, paths.MetadataFileName)\n\t\tif metaEntry, metaExists := entries[metaPath]; metaExists {\n\t\t\tmeta, metaErr := s.readMetadataFromBlob(metaEntry.Hash)\n\t\t\tif metaErr == nil && meta.SessionID == opts.SessionID {\n\t\t\t\tsessionIndex = i\n\t\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif sessionIndex == -1 {\n\t\t// Fall back to latest session; log so mismatches are diagnosable.\n\t\tsessionIndex = len(checkpointSummary.Sessions) - 1\n\t\tlogging.Debug(ctx, \"UpdateCommitted: session ID not found, falling back to latest\",\n\t\t\tslog.String(\"session_id\", opts.SessionID),\n\t\t\tslog.String(\"checkpoint_id\", string(opts.CheckpointID)),\n\t\t\tslog.Int(\"fallback_index\", sessionIndex),\n\t\t)\n\t}\n\n\tsessionPath := fmt.Sprintf(\"%s%d/\", basePath, sessionIndex)\n\n\t// Replace transcript (full replace, not append)\n\tif len(opts.Transcript) > 0 {\n\t\tif err := s.replaceTranscript(opts.Transcript, sessionPath, entries); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to replace transcript: %w\", err)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Replace prompts\n\tif len(opts.Prompts) > 0 {\n\t\tpromptContent := strings.Join(opts.Prompts, \"\\n\\n---\\n\\n\")\n\t\tblobHash, err := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, []byte(promptContent))\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to create prompt blob: %w\", err)\n\t\t}\n\t\tentries[sessionPath+paths.PromptFileName] = object.TreeEntry{\n\t\t\tName: sessionPath + paths.PromptFileName,\n\t\t\tMode: filemode.Regular,\n\t\t\tHash: blobHash,\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Replace context\n\tif len(opts.Context) > 0 {\n\t\tcontextBlob, err := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, opts.Context)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to create context blob: %w\", err)\n\t\t}\n\t\tentries[sessionPath+paths.ContextFileName] = object.TreeEntry{\n\t\t\tName: sessionPath + paths.ContextFileName,\n\t\t\tMode: filemode.Regular,\n\t\t\tHash: contextBlob,\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Build and commit\n\tnewTreeHash, err := BuildTreeFromEntries(s.repo, entries)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tauthorName, authorEmail := getGitAuthorFromRepo(s.repo)\n\tcommitMsg := fmt.Sprintf(\"Finalize transcript for checkpoint %s\", opts.CheckpointID)\n\tnewCommitHash, err := s.createCommit(newTreeHash, ref.Hash(), commitMsg, authorName, authorEmail)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\trefName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName)\n\tnewRef := plumbing.NewHashReference(refName, newCommitHash)\n\tif err := s.repo.Storer.SetReference(newRef); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to set branch reference: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// replaceTranscript writes the full transcript content, replacing any existing transcript.\n// Also removes any chunk files from a previous write and updates the content hash.\nfunc (s *GitStore) replaceTranscript(transcript []byte, sessionPath string, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry) error {\n\t// Remove existing transcript files (base + any chunks)\n\ttranscriptBase := sessionPath + paths.TranscriptFileName\n\tfor key := range entries {\n\t\tif key == transcriptBase || strings.HasPrefix(key, transcriptBase+\".\") {\n\t\t\tdelete(entries, key)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Write new transcript blob\n\tblobHash, err := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, transcript)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to create transcript blob: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tentries[transcriptBase] = object.TreeEntry{\n\t\tName: transcriptBase,\n\t\tMode: filemode.Regular,\n\t\tHash: blobHash,\n\t}\n\n\t// Update content hash\n\tcontentHash := fmt.Sprintf(\"sha256:%x\", sha256.Sum256(transcript))\n\thashBlob, err := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, []byte(contentHash))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to create content hash blob: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\thashPath := sessionPath + paths.ContentHashFileName\n\tentries[hashPath] = object.TreeEntry{\n\t\tName: hashPath,\n\t\tMode: filemode.Regular,\n\t\tHash: hashBlob,\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// ensureSessionsBranch ensures the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch exists.\nfunc (s *GitStore) ensureSessionsBranch() error {"
}

   313→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(shadowRef)

   327→	// Extract transcript — prefer the live file when available, fall back to shadow branch.

   329→	// (SaveChanges is only called when there are file modifications).

   341→			}

   345→			}

   347→	}

   352→		data.FullTranscriptLines = countTranscriptItems(agentType, fullTranscript)
   353→		data.Prompts = extractUserPrompts(agentType, fullTranscript)
   354→		data.Context = generateContextFromPrompts(data.Prompts)

   368→// countTranscriptItems counts lines (JSONL) or messages (JSON) in a transcript.
   369→// For Claude Code and JSONL-based agents, this counts lines.
   370→// For Gemini CLI and JSON-based agents, this counts messages.
   371→// Returns 0 if the content is empty or malformed.
   372→func countTranscriptItems(agentType agent.AgentType, content string) int {
   373→	if content == "" {
   374→		return 0
   375→	}
   376→
   377→	// Try Gemini format first if agentType is Gemini, or as fallback if Unknown
   378→	if agentType == agent.AgentTypeGemini || agentType == agent.AgentTypeUnknown {
   379→		transcript, err := geminicli.ParseTranscript([]byte(content))
   380→		if err == nil && transcript != nil && len(transcript.Messages) > 0 {
   381→			return len(transcript.Messages)
   382→		}
   383→		// If agentType is explicitly Gemini but parsing failed, return 0
   384→		if agentType == agent.AgentTypeGemini {
   385→			return 0
   386→		}
   387→		// Otherwise fall through to JSONL parsing for Unknown type
   388→	}
   389→
   390→	// Claude Code and other JSONL-based agents
   391→	allLines := strings.Split(content, "\n")
   392→	// Trim trailing empty lines (from final \n in JSONL)
   393→	for len(allLines) > 0 && strings.TrimSpace(allLines[len(allLines)-1]) == "" {
   394→		allLines = allLines[:len(allLines)-1]
   395→	}
   396→	return len(allLines)
   397→}

   414→					cleaned = append(cleaned, stripped)
   415→				}
   416→			}

   418→		}

   420→		if agentType == agent.AgentTypeGemini {
   421→			return nil
   422→		}
   423→		// Otherwise fall through to JSONL parsing for Unknown type
   424→	}
   425→
   426→	// Claude Code and other JSONL-based agents

HandleTurnEnd replaces that with the complete session transcript\n// (from prompt to stop event), ensuring every checkpoint has the full context.\n//\n//nolint:unparam // error return required by interface but hooks must return nil\nfunc (s *ManualCommitStrategy) HandleTurnEnd(state *SessionState, _ []session.Action) error {\n\t// Finalize all checkpoints from this turn with the full transcript.\n\t// Best-effort: log warnings but don't fail the hook.\n\ts.finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints(state)\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints replaces the provisional transcript in each checkpoint\n// created during this turn with the full session transcript.\n//\n// This is called at turn end (stop hook). During the turn, PostCommit wrote whatever\n// transcript was available at commit time. Now we have the complete transcript and\n// replace it so every checkpoint has the full prompt-to-stop context.\nfunc (s *ManualCommitStrategy) finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints(state *SessionState) {\n\tif len(state.TurnCheckpointIDs) == 0 {\n\t\treturn // No mid-turn commits to finalize\n\t}\n\n\tlogCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), \"checkpoint\")\n\n\tlogging.Info(logCtx, \"finalizing turn checkpoints with full transcript\",\n\t\tslog.String(\"session_id\", state.SessionID),\n\t\tslog.Int(\"checkpoint_count\", len(state.TurnCheckpointIDs)),\n\t)\n\n\t// Read full transcript from live transcript file\n\tif state.TranscriptPath == \"\" {\n\t\tlogging.Warn(logCtx, \"finalize: no transcript path, skipping\",\n\t\t\tslog.String(\"session_id\", state.SessionID),\n\t\t)\n\t\tstate.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tfullTranscript, err := os.ReadFile(state.TranscriptPath) //nolint:gosec // path from session state\n\tif err != nil || len(fullTranscript) == 0 {\n\t\tlogging.Warn(logCtx, \"finalize: failed to read transcript, skipping\",\n\t\t\tslog.String(\"session_id\", state.SessionID),\n\t\t\tslog.String(\"transcript_path\", state.TranscriptPath),\n\t\t)\n\t\tstate.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\t// Extract prompts and context from the full transcript\n\tprompts := extractUserPrompts(state.AgentType, string(fullTranscript))\n\tcontextBytes := generateContextFromPrompts(prompts)\n\n\t// Open repository and create checkpoint store\n\trepo, err := OpenRepository()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tlogging.Warn(logCtx, \"finalize: failed to open repository\",\n\t\t\tslog.String(\"error\", err.Error()),\n\t\t)\n\t\tstate.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tstore := checkpoint.NewGitStore(repo)\n\n\t// Update each checkpoint with the full transcript\n\tfor _, cpIDStr := range state.TurnCheckpointIDs {\n\t\tcpID, parseErr := id.NewCheckpointID(cpIDStr)\n\t\tif parseErr != nil {\n\t\t\tlogging.Warn(logCtx, \"finalize: invalid checkpoint ID, skipping\",\n\t\t\t\tslog.String(\"checkpoint_id\", cpIDStr),\n\t\t\t\tslog.String(\"error\", parseErr.Error()),\n\t\t\t)\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tupdateErr := store.UpdateCommitted(context.Background(), checkpoint.UpdateCommittedOptions{\n\t\t\tCheckpointID: cpID,\n\t\t\tSessionID:    state.SessionID,\n\t\t\tTranscript:   fullTranscript,\n\t\t\tPrompts:      prompts,\n\t\t\tContext:      contextBytes,\n\t\t})\n\t\tif updateErr != nil {\n\t\t\tlogging.Warn(logCtx, \"finalize: failed to update checkpoint\",\n\t\t\t\tslog.String(\"checkpoint_id\", cpIDStr),\n\t\t\t\tslog.String(\"error\", updateErr.Error()),\n\t\t\t)\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tlogging.Info(logCtx, \"finalize: checkpoint updated with full transcript\",\n\t\t\tslog.String(\"checkpoint_id\", cpIDStr),\n\t\t\tslog.String(\"session_id\", state.SessionID),\n\t\t)\n\t}\n\n\t// Update transcript start and clear turn checkpoint IDs\n\tfullTranscriptLines := countTranscriptItems(state.AgentType, string(fullTranscript))\n\tstate.CheckpointTranscriptStart = fullTranscriptLines\n\tstate.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil\n}"

question: what happens now if I press `ctrl+c` after the agent made the first commit

> AGENT

Good question. Two scenarios:

**Graceful ctrl+c (stop hook fires):**
The stop hook triggers `EventTurnEnd` → `HandleTurnEnd` → `finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints`. It reads the full transcript, updates the checkpoint with it, clears `TurnCheckpointIDs`. Everything works as designed.

**Hard kill / crash (stop hook doesn't fire):**
`TurnCheckpointIDs = ["cp1"]` persists in the state file. On next prompt, `InitializeSession` runs and clears it:

```go
state.LastCheckpointID = ""
state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
```

The checkpoint "cp1" permanently keeps its **provisional transcript** — whatever was available at commit time. It won't get the post-commit conversation (agent explaining what it did, etc.).

**Is this a problem?** The provisional transcript already contains everything from session start through the commit, so it's incomplete but not empty. For a crash scenario, that's reasonable degradation.

**Possible improvement:** InitializeSession could try to finalize before clearing — check if `TurnCheckpointIDs` is non-empty and attempt `finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints` with whatever transcript is available. This would recover the post-commit portion if the transcript file still exists. Want me to add that?

    20→// pushSessionsBranchCommon is the shared implementation for pushing session branches.
    21→// Used by both manual-commit and auto-commit strategies.
    22→// By default, session logs are pushed automatically alongside user pushes.
    23→// Configuration (stored in .entire/settings.json under strategy_options.push_sessions):

    26→func pushSessionsBranchCommon(remote, branchName string) error {
    27→	// Check if pushing is disabled
    28→	if isPushSessionsDisabled() {
    29→		return nil
    30→	}
    31→
    32→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
    33→	if err != nil {

    37→	// Check if branch exists locally

    39→	localRef, err := repo.Reference(branchRef, true)

    41→		// No branch, nothing to push

    43→	}
    44→
    45→	// Check if there's actually something to push (local differs from remote)
    46→	if !hasUnpushedSessionsCommon(repo, remote, localRef.Hash(), branchName) {
    47→		// Nothing to push - skip silently
    48→		return nil
    49→	}

    54→// hasUnpushedSessionsCommon checks if the local branch differs from the remote.
    55→// Returns true if there's any difference that needs syncing (local ahead, remote ahead, or diverged).
    56→func hasUnpushedSessionsCommon(repo *git.Repository, remote string, localHash plumbing.Hash, branchName string) bool {
    57→	// Check for remote tracking ref: refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>
    58→	remoteRefName := plumbing.NewRemoteReferenceName(remote, branchName)

    62→		return true
    63→	}
    64→

    66→	// This is the only case where we skip - any difference needs handling
    67→	return localHash != remoteRef.Hash()

   105→// tryPushSessionsCommon attempts to push the sessions branch.
   106→func tryPushSessionsCommon(remote, branchName string) error {
   107→	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Minute)
   108→	defer cancel()
   109→
   110→	// Use --no-verify to prevent recursive hook calls
   111→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "push", "--no-verify", remote, branchName)
   112→	cmd.Stdin = nil // Disconnect stdin to prevent hanging in hook context

   114→	output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
   115→	if err != nil {

   117→		if strings.Contains(string(output), "non-fast-forward") ||
   118→			strings.Contains(string(output), "rejected") {
   119→			return errors.New("non-fast-forward")
   120→		}
   121→		return fmt.Errorf("push failed: %s", output)
   122→	}
   123→	return nil

   126→// fetchAndMergeSessionsCommon fetches remote sessions and merges into local using go-git.
   127→// Since session logs are append-only (unique cond-* directories), we just combine trees.
   128→func fetchAndMergeSessionsCommon(remote, branchName string) error {
   129→	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Minute)
   130→	defer cancel()
   131→
   132→	// Use git CLI for fetch (go-git's fetch can be tricky with auth)

   135→	if output, err := fetchCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
   136→		return fmt.Errorf("fetch failed: %s", output)

   146→	if err != nil {

   148→	}

   150→	if err != nil {
   151→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get local commit: %w", err)
   152→	}
   153→	localTree, err := localCommit.Tree()
   154→	if err != nil {
   155→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get local tree: %w", err)
   156→	}
   157→
   158→	// Get remote (FETCH_HEAD)
   159→	fetchHeadRef, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.ReferenceName("FETCH_HEAD"), true)
   160→	if err != nil {
   161→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get FETCH_HEAD: %w", err)
   162→	}
   163→	remoteCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(fetchHeadRef.Hash())
   164→	if err != nil {
   165→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get remote commit: %w", err)
   166→	}
   167→	remoteTree, err := remoteCommit.Tree()
   168→	if err != nil {
   169→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get remote tree: %w", err)
   170→	}
   171→
   172→	// Flatten both trees and combine entries
   173→	// Session logs have unique cond-* directories, so no conflicts expected
   174→	entries := make(map[string]object.TreeEntry)
   175→	if err := checkpoint.FlattenTree(repo, localTree, "", entries); err != nil {
   176→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to flatten local tree: %w", err)
   177→	}
   178→	if err := checkpoint.FlattenTree(repo, remoteTree, "", entries); err != nil {
   179→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to flatten remote tree: %w", err)
   180→	}
   181→
   182→	// Build merged tree
   183→	mergedTreeHash, err := checkpoint.BuildTreeFromEntries(repo, entries)
   184→	if err != nil {
   185→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to build merged tree: %w", err)
   186→	}
   187→
   188→	// Create merge commit with both parents
   189→	mergeCommitHash, err := createMergeCommitCommon(repo, mergedTreeHash,
   190→		[]plumbing.Hash{localRef.Hash(), fetchHeadRef.Hash()},
   191→		"Merge remote session logs")
   192→	if err != nil {
   193→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create merge commit: %w", err)
   194→	}
   195→
   196→	// Update branch ref
   197→	newRef := plumbing.NewHashReference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(branchName), mergeCommitHash)
   198→	if err := repo.Storer.SetReference(newRef); err != nil {
   199→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to update branch ref: %w", err)
   200→	}
   201→
   202→	return nil
   203→}

   205→// createMergeCommitCommon creates a merge commit with multiple parents.
   206→func createMergeCommitCommon(repo *git.Repository, treeHash plumbing.Hash, parents []plumbing.Hash, message string) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   207→	authorName, authorEmail := GetGitAuthorFromRepo(repo)
   208→	now := time.Now()
   209→	sig := object.Signature{
   210→		Name:  authorName,
   211→		Email: authorEmail,
   212→		When:  now,
   213→	}
   214→

   217→		ParentHashes: parents,
   218→		Author:       sig,
   219→		Committer:    sig,
   220→		Message:      message,
   221→	}
   222→
   223→	obj := repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
   224→	if err := commit.Encode(obj); err != nil {
   225→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to encode commit: %w", err)
   226→	}
   227→
   228→	hash, err := repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(obj)
   229→	if err != nil {
   230→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to store commit: %w", err)
   231→	}
   232→
   233→	return hash, nil
   234→}

> AGENT

The push mid-turn is fine **for the push itself** — it just pushes `entire/checkpoints/v1` alongside the user branch. But the issue you're getting at:

**The pushed checkpoint has the provisional transcript, not the full one.**

Here's the timeline:

1. Agent commits → PostCommit condenses provisional transcript to `entire/checkpoints/v1` locally
2. Agent pushes → PrePush pushes `entire/checkpoints/v1` to remote (with provisional transcript)
3. Agent finishes → HandleTurnEnd calls `UpdateCommitted` (replaces with full transcript) — **but only locally**

The remote now has the provisional transcript permanently. The finalized version only exists locally until the *next* push.

This is probably fine in practice — the next push will update the remote. But there's a window where the remote has an incomplete transcript. Worth noting but not necessarily worth fixing, since:
- The provisional transcript already has everything up to commit time
- The next push overwrites it
- Pre-push is best-effort anyway (failures don't block the push)

**Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES**

### Previous Review Status

3 of 5 issues from review-01 are fixed:

### Critical Finding

**`condensed` flag is set to `true` even when condensation fails.** At `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:564-565` and `:577-578`, the code calls `condenseAndUpdateState()` and then unconditionally sets `condensed = true` on the next line. However, `condenseAndUpdateState` can fail silently (returns void, logs a warning, and returns early). The stale docstring on line 649 says "Returns true if condensation succeeded" but the function has no return value.

This causes three problems on condensation failure:
1. A never-written checkpoint ID gets appended to `TurnCheckpointIDs`, causing `ErrCheckpointNotFound` noise at turn end
2. `carryForwardToNewShadowBranch` runs with the old `BaseCommit` (not updated since condensation failed), potentially creating a shadow branch that collides with the existing one
3. The session is not tracked in `uncondensedActiveOnBranch` (happens to be safe by accident since the shadow branch is also not in `shadowBranchesToDelete`)

**Fix:** Make `condenseAndUpdateState` return a `bool` indicating success, and only set `condensed = true` when it returns `true`.

### Important Findings

- **Transcript file lifetime risk**: `finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints` reads from `state.TranscriptPath` at stop time. If the agent process has already cleaned up its temp files, all mid-turn checkpoints will permanently have incomplete transcripts.
- **docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md:11** still references `PendingCheckpointID` (carried over from review-01).
- **auto_commit.go** generates `TurnID` but never uses it -- dead data in session state.

---

## Architecture Review: `soph/one-to-one-checkpoints` vs `main`

### 1. Architecture Overview

This branch replaces the previous N:1 checkpoint model (multiple commits could share one checkpoint ID via `LastCheckpointID` reuse) with a 1:1 model (every commit gets its own unique checkpoint). The core idea is "provisional-then-finalize": at commit time (PostCommit hook), checkpoint data is condensed immediately with whatever transcript is available; at stop time (HandleTurnEnd), the provisional transcript is replaced with the complete session transcript.

The changes span four architectural layers:
- **State machine** (`session/phase.go`): Removed `ACTIVE_COMMITTED` phase, simplifying from 4 to 3 phases
- **Checkpoint store** (`checkpoint/committed.go`): New `UpdateCommitted` method for in-place transcript replacement
- **Hook orchestration** (`strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go`): Single-pass PostCommit with carry-forward, finalization at turn end
- **Session state** (`session/state.go`): New `TurnCheckpointIDs` and `TurnID` fields

---

### 2. Change Assessment

**What works well:**

The state machine simplification is architecturally sound. Removing `ACTIVE_COMMITTED` eliminates a complex intermediate state, the two-pass PostCommit architecture, and the `ActionMigrateShadowBranch` action. The 1:1 model is conceptually cleaner and eliminates an entire class of bugs around checkpoint ID reuse and `PendingCheckpointID` lifetime management.

The carry-forward mechanism (`carryForwardToNewShadowBranch`) is well-designed: it computes `subtractFiles(filesTouchedBefore, committedFileSet)` and creates a new shadow branch for remaining files, allowing the next commit to get its own checkpoint. The helper functions `filesChangedInCommit` and `subtractFiles` are clean, testable abstractions.

The `UpdateCommitted` method on `GitStore` follows the existing patterns well -- it reads the current tree entries, modifies the relevant blobs, rebuilds the tree, and commits. The fallback-to-latest-session logic with debug logging is pragmatic.

**However, there is a critical data flow issue.**

---

### 3. Compliance Check

**CRITICAL: HandleTurnEnd is never called -- finalization is dead code**

The provisional-then-finalize architecture has a severed data flow path. Here is the chain:

1. PostCommit records checkpoint IDs in `state.TurnCheckpointIDs` (line 599-600 of `manual_commit_hooks.go`)
2. `HandleTurnEnd` calls `finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints` which reads `state.TurnCheckpointIDs` and calls `store.UpdateCommitted` for each (lines 1323-1417)
3. `HandleTurnEnd` is called from `transitionSessionTurnEnd` in `hooks_claudecode_handlers.go` (line 761)
4. BUT `transitionSessionTurnEnd` guards the call: `if len(remaining) > 0` (line 758)
5. The `ACTIVE + TurnEnd` transition (line 185-189 of `phase.go`) emits only `ActionUpdateLastInteraction`
6. `ActionUpdateLastInteraction` is consumed by `ApplyCommonActions` (line 263)
7. Therefore `remaining` is always empty for `ACTIVE + TurnEnd`
8. `HandleTurnEnd` is never called

This means **every mid-turn checkpoint will permanently contain only the provisional (partial) transcript**. The "full context" finalization documented throughout the code and `summary.md` will never execute.

The test `TestTurnEnd_Active_NoActions` (line 613 of `phase_postcommit_test.go`) directly calls `HandleTurnEnd` with empty actions and asserts it is "a no-op", which is correct for the no-`TurnCheckpointIDs` case. But there is no test that exercises the actual data flow: `PostCommit` records IDs into `TurnCheckpointIDs`, then `transitionSessionTurnEnd` invokes `HandleTurnEnd` to finalize them. Such a test would fail because the guard prevents the call.

**Fix options:**

(a) Change the `ACTIVE + TurnEnd` transition to emit a new action (e.g., `ActionFinalizeTranscripts`) that passes through `ApplyCommonActions` to `remaining`, enabling the `HandleTurnEnd` call.

(b) Change `transitionSessionTurnEnd` to always call `HandleTurnEnd` regardless of remaining actions, since `HandleTurnEnd` now reads its work items from `state.TurnCheckpointIDs` rather than from the action list.

(c) Call `finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints` directly from `transitionSessionTurnEnd` or `commitWithMetadata`, bypassing the `TurnEndHandler` interface entirely.

Option (b) is the most architecturally consistent with the new design, since `HandleTurnEnd` ignores the actions parameter (uses `_`) and drives entirely from `state.TurnCheckpointIDs`.

---

**SOLID Principles:**

- **Single Responsibility**: Generally upheld. The `checkpoint` package handles storage, `session` handles state machine, `strategy` handles orchestration. The `sessionid` package extraction is a good example of narrowing responsibility.

- **Open/Closed**: The `Store` interface addition (`UpdateCommitted`) is additive but constitutes a breaking change for any hypothetical alternative implementations. Since `GitStore` is the sole implementation (verified by `var _ Store = (*GitStore)(nil)` in `store.go`), this is pragmatically fine but should be noted for future extensibility.

- **Interface Segregation**: The `TurnEndHandler` optional interface pattern is well-applied. The auto-commit strategy does not implement it, so it is not forced to handle turn-end actions it does not need.

- **Dependency Inversion**: The `sessionid` package correctly avoids import cycles by having minimal dependencies, consistent with the documented `settings` package pattern.

---

**Backward Compatibility:**

- `PhaseActiveCommitted` ("active_committed") gracefully degrades to `PhaseIdle` via `PhaseFromString`, which is the correct fallback for sessions created by older CLI versions. This is well-handled.

- The `PendingCheckpointID` field removal is safe because the field was only read from in-process state (never persisted cross-version), and old state files with the field will simply ignore it via `json:"...,omitempty"`.

- The `TurnCheckpointIDs` field uses `omitempty`, so old CLI versions reading new state files will simply not see it. New CLI versions reading old state files will see it as nil/empty. Both directions are safe.

- Session ID format change (dropping date prefix to identity function) has backward compatibility via `ModelSessionID` which strips the prefix if present.

---

### 4. Risk Analysis

**High Risk:**

1. **Dead finalization path** (detailed above). Every checkpoint created during an active turn will contain an incomplete transcript. Users querying checkpoint history will get truncated session context, which defeats the stated purpose of the branch.

**Medium Risk:**

2. **Carry-forward atomicity**: `carryForwardToNewShadowBranch` (line 608-632 of `manual_commit_hooks.go`) writes a new shadow branch entry and then updates `state.FilesTouched`, `state.StepCount`, etc. If the process crashes between `WriteTemporary` succeeding and `saveSessionState` succeeding, the shadow branch will exist but the state file will not reflect the carry-forward. The next PostCommit will see stale state. However, this is a pre-existing pattern (the same race exists with the regular `SaveChanges` path), and the system is designed for best-effort behavior in hooks.

3. **N+1 git commits on metadata branch during finalization**: `finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints` calls `store.UpdateCommitted` for each checkpoint sequentially. Each call creates a new commit on `entire/checkpoints/v1`. For a turn with 5 mid-turn commits, this creates 5 sequential commits on the metadata branch. This is functionally correct but could be optimized to batch all updates into a single commit.

**Low Risk:**

4. **`EnsureSetup` moved from `captureInitialState` to `commitWithMetadata`**: Git hooks are no longer installed at turn start. They are installed at commit time (`commitWithMetadata`) and subagent checkpoint time (`handleClaudeCodePostTodo`, `handleClaudeCodePostTask`). If the agent makes its first commit without going through these code paths (e.g., via raw `git commit`), hooks might not be installed. However, the manual-commit strategy's `EnsureSetup` in `manual_commit.go` also checks/installs hooks, so this is likely covered through multiple call sites.

5. **Auto-commit strategy adds `TurnID` but does not add `TurnCheckpointIDs` or `UpdateCommitted` support**: The auto-commit strategy sets `TurnID` in `InitializeSession` but does not implement `TurnEndHandler` and does not populate `TurnCheckpointIDs`. This is consistent with the auto-commit design where commits are made on the active branch by the strategy itself (not via user git hooks), so the provisional-then-finalize pattern does not apply. This is architecturally correct but the asymmetry should be documented.

---

### 5. Recommendations

**Must fix before merge:**

1. **Fix the `HandleTurnEnd` invocation path.** The `if len(remaining) > 0` guard in `transitionSessionTurnEnd` (`/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/hooks_claudecode_handlers.go`, line 758) prevents `HandleTurnEnd` from being called when `ACTIVE + TurnEnd` produces no strategy-specific actions. The simplest fix: remove the guard and always call `HandleTurnEnd` when the strategy implements `TurnEndHandler`, since `HandleTurnEnd` now drives from `state.TurnCheckpointIDs` rather than from the action list. Alternatively, add a new action to the `ACTIVE + TurnEnd` transition.

2. **Add an integration test for the full finalization flow.** The test should: (a) start a session, (b) make mid-turn commit, (c) verify `TurnCheckpointIDs` is populated, (d) simulate stop/turn-end, (e) verify the checkpoint transcript was updated from provisional to full. This test would have caught the dead code path.

**Should fix:**

3. **Batch `UpdateCommitted` calls.** In `finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints`, each checkpoint update creates a separate commit on the metadata branch. Consider adding a batch variant that updates multiple checkpoints in a single tree-rebuild-and-commit cycle.

4. **Document the auto-commit asymmetry.** The auto-commit strategy now sets `TurnID` but does not participate in the provisional-then-finalize flow. A brief comment in `auto_commit.go` explaining why would help future maintainers.

5. **Remove `summary.md` from the branch.** It appears to be a session summary artifact (listed as untracked in `git status`), not intended for the repository.

**Consider:**

6. **Rename `HandleTurnEnd` to `FinalizeTurnCheckpoints` or similar.** The current name suggests it dispatches arbitrary turn-end actions, but the new implementation ignores the action parameter and has a single purpose: transcript finalization. A more specific name would make the contract clearer.

7. **The `TurnEndHandler` interface comment** at `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/strategy.go` (line 460-469) still says "dispatches strategy-specific actions emitted by the turn-end transition" but the implementation ignores the actions parameter. The interface contract and its documentation should be updated to reflect that the handler reads its work items from session state, not from the action list.

> AGENT

All tests pass. Let me summarize the two fixes:

**Fix 1 — HandleTurnEnd was never called (CRITICAL):**
- `ACTIVE + TurnEnd` emits only `ActionUpdateLastInteraction`, which `ApplyCommonActions` consumes, leaving `remaining` empty
- The `if len(remaining) > 0` guard in `transitionSessionTurnEnd` prevented `HandleTurnEnd` from ever being called
- Removed the guard — `HandleTurnEnd` is now always called when the strategy implements `TurnEndHandler`, since it reads work items from `state.TurnCheckpointIDs` rather than from the action list

**Fix 2 — `condensed` flag set even on failure:**
- `condenseAndUpdateState` returned `void` but `condensed = true` was set unconditionally after the call
- Changed it to return `bool` — returns `false` on failure, `true` on success
- Both call sites now use `condensed = s.condenseAndUpdateState(...)` so phantom checkpoint IDs can't leak into `TurnCheckpointIDs`

Both fixes are clean — format, lint, and all tests (unit + integration) pass.

> DEVELOPER

1. condenseAndUpdateState returning bool — Without this, failed condensation incorrectly records checkpoint IDs in TurnCheckpointIDs and triggers carry-forward.
  2. Removing the if len(remaining) > 0 guard on HandleTurnEnd — Without this, HandleTurnEnd is never called because ACTIVE → IDLE produces no remaining actions after ApplyCommonActions. The entire finalization mechanism silently doesn't work.

> AGENT

Yep, both are fixed and all tests pass. Those were the two critical bugs from the reviews — the finalization path is now actually reachable, and phantom checkpoint IDs can no longer leak through failed condensation.

> DEVELOPER

Flagged by both the code quality reviewer and data integrity guardian independently.

  WriteCommitted applies redact.JSONLBytes() to transcripts and redact.String() to prompts. But UpdateCommitted / replaceTranscript writes raw bytes without redaction. Since finalization replaces the redacted content with the full transcript from disk, secrets that were stripped during initial condensation get
  re-exposed on entire/checkpoints/v1.

  Fix: Apply redaction in finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints before passing data to UpdateCommitted, or inside replaceTranscript itself.

```
     1→# Known Limitations
     2→
     3→This document describes known limitations of the Entire CLI.
     4→
     5→## Git Operations
     6→
     7→### Amending Commits with `-m` Flag
     8→
     9→When you amend a commit using `git commit --amend -m "new message"`, the `-m` flag replaces the entire message including any `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer. Git passes `source="message"` (not `"commit"`) to the prepare-commit-msg hook, so the amend-specific trailer preservation logic is bypassed.
    10→
    11→**However, the trailer is automatically restored** if `PendingCheckpointID` or `LastCheckpointID` exists in session state (set during the original condensation). This means `git commit --amend -m "..."` preserves the checkpoint link in most cases, including when Claude does the amend in a non-interactive environment.
    12→
    13→The only case where the link is lost is when `-m` is used with genuinely *new* content (no prior condensation) and `/dev/tty` is not available for the interactive confirmation prompt.
    14→
    15→**Tracked in:** [ENT-161](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-161)
    16→
    17→### Git GC Can Corrupt Worktree Indexes
    18→
    19→When using git worktrees, `git gc --auto` can corrupt a worktree's index by pruning loose objects that the worktree's index cache-tree references. This manifests as:
    20→
    21→```
    22→fatal: unable to read <hash>
    23→error: invalid sha1 pointer in cache-tree of .git/worktrees/<n>/index
    24→```
    25→
    26→**Root cause:** Checkpoint saves use go-git's `SetEncodedObject` which creates loose objects. When the count exceeds the `gc.auto` threshold (default 6700), any git operation (e.g., VS Code or Sourcetree background fetch) triggers `git gc --auto`. GC doesn't fully account for worktree index references when pruning, so objects get deleted while the worktree index still points to them.
    27→
    28→**Impact:**
    29→- `git status` fails in the affected worktree
    30→- Staged changes in the worktree are lost
    31→
    32→**Recovery:**
    33→```bash
    34→# In the affected worktree:
    35→git read-tree HEAD
    36→```
    37→This rebuilds the index from HEAD. Any previously staged changes will need to be re-staged.
    38→
    39→**Prevention:** Disable auto-GC and run it manually after commits (when indexes are clean):
    40→```bash
    41→git config gc.auto 0
    42→```
    43→
    44→**Tracked in:** [ENT-241](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-241)
    45→

> AGENT

The right fix: `ACTIVE_COMMITTED` should normalize to `ACTIVE`, not `IDLE`. In the old model `ACTIVE_COMMITTED` meant "agent is still active, a commit happened mid-turn." The agent was still running. Normalizing to `ACTIVE` preserves that — the next `TurnEnd` event will fire `HandleTurnEnd` and finalize any pending checkpoints. Normalizing to `IDLE` silently drops that.

> DEVELOPER

how do we update the checkpoints at the end of a turn, we ammend the commit?

> AGENT

No, we don't touch the user's commits at all. The checkpoints live on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` orphan branch — a completely separate branch that never shares history with the user's working branch.

`UpdateCommitted` reads the existing tree on that orphan branch, replaces the transcript/prompts/context blobs for the given checkpoint ID, then creates a new commit on `entire/checkpoints/v1`. The user's branch and commit history are untouched.

> DEVELOPER

yeah I mean the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch, so a checkpoint folder has multiple commits now?

> AGENT

No, each checkpoint folder (`a3/b2c4d5e6f7/`) still has exactly one version at any point in time — the latest tree on `entire/checkpoints/v1` is the source of truth.

`UpdateCommitted` does a full tree replace: it reads the current tree, swaps the blobs for that checkpoint's session folder, and creates a new commit on the branch. So the branch gains an extra commit, but the tree only ever has one version of each checkpoint's content. The old (provisional) content is only reachable by walking the branch's git history — it's not a separate folder or duplicate.

So: one folder per checkpoint, one commit at condensation time (provisional transcript), one more commit at turn end (full transcript). The second overwrites the first in the tree.

> DEVELOPER

I understand how git works, but we are not replacing the initial commit, we are updating with a second commit

> AGENT

You're right — that's the N+1 commits issue the performance review flagged. Each `UpdateCommitted` call adds another commit to `entire/checkpoints/v1`. With 3 mid-turn commits you get 3 provisional commits at condensation time, then 3 more finalization commits at turn end. Six commits for what could be four (3 provisional + 1 batch finalization).

Want me to batch the finalization so `finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints` does a single tree rebuild across all checkpoint IDs and creates one commit?

Updated both CLAUDE.md and the architecture doc. Removed "Approach B" (commit message search) since the CLI only uses tree-at-HEAD lookup, and added a note that commit subjects are for human `git log` readability only.

> DEVELOPER

does this introduce any more risk when merging the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch with upstream changes? risk of conflicts?

> AGENT

No additional conflict risk. Checkpoint IDs are random 12-hex-char values, so different developers always write to different sharded paths (`a3/b2c4d5e6f7/` vs `d4/e5f6a7b8c9d0/`). The finalization commit modifies the same path as the provisional commit, but no other developer would ever touch that same path.

The only existing risk is non-fast-forward pushes — two developers pushing `entire/checkpoints/v1` at the same time. The finalization commits add more commits to the branch, which slightly widens the window for that race, but the content will always merge cleanly since the paths don't overlap.

> AGENT

You can't use interactive rebase for this since `entire/checkpoints/v1` is an orphan branch with potentially many commits. `git filter-branch` or `git filter-repo` would be the right tools:

```bash
# Using git filter-repo (preferred, faster):
git filter-repo --path summary.md --invert-paths --refs entire/checkpoints/v1

# Using git filter-branch (built-in):
git filter-branch --tree-filter 'rm -f summary.md' -- entire/checkpoints/v1
```

It was added in `248c9ae9`. That's 3 commits back. Here's the interactive rebase command:

```bash
git rebase -i 248c9ae9~1
```

That will open an editor with commits from `248c9ae9` onward. Mark `248c9ae9` as `edit`, then:

```bash
git rm summary.md
git commit --amend --no-edit
git rebase --continue
```

But since this is a shared branch that's been pushed, this rewrites history for all 3 commits. Are you sure you want to do this, or would you rather just `git rm summary.md` in a new commit?

## 1:1 Checkpoint-to-Commit Mapping with Deferred Transcript Finalization

### Problem

Previously, checkpoints used a 1:N model — one checkpoint ID could span multiple commits. When an agent made several commits during a single turn, they all shared the same checkpoint ID. This made it impossible to tie a specific commit to a specific snapshot of session context, and the `ACTIVE_COMMITTED` phase added complexity to the state machine.

### Approach

Every user commit now gets its own unique checkpoint ID. The core challenge is that mid-turn commits happen before the agent is done — the transcript is incomplete. We solve this with a **provisional-then-finalize** pattern:

1. **At commit time (PostCommit hook):** Condense whatever transcript exists so far to `entire/checkpoints/v1` with a fresh checkpoint ID. This is *provisional* — the transcript is partial. Then carry forward any remaining uncommitted files to a new shadow branch so the next commit gets its own checkpoint.

2. **At turn end (Stop hook):** `HandleTurnEnd` iterates over all checkpoint IDs recorded during the turn (`TurnCheckpointIDs` on session state) and replaces each provisional transcript with the complete one via `UpdateCommitted`.

This means every checkpoint on `entire/checkpoints/v1` ends up with the full prompt-to-stop transcript, while each commit still gets its own unique ID for precise linking.

### Key changes

**New: `UpdateCommitted` on checkpoint store**
- Replace semantics (not append) — swaps transcript, prompts, and context blobs for a checkpoint's session folder
- Chunks large transcripts (matching `WriteCommitted` behavior)
- Redacts secrets before writing (matching `WriteCommitted` behavior)

**New: `TurnCheckpointIDs` on session state**
- Tracks checkpoint IDs condensed during the current agent turn
- Populated in PostCommit for ACTIVE sessions after successful condensation
- Consumed in `HandleTurnEnd` to finalize all checkpoints
- Cleared on new prompt (both strategies)

**New: `HandleTurnEnd` finalization**
- `TurnEndHandler` interface simplified — no longer takes `[]session.Action` parameter since work items come from state, not the action list
- Called unconditionally when strategy implements the interface (removed dead `if len(remaining) > 0` guard)

**Phase simplification**
- Removed `ACTIVE_COMMITTED` phase — the state machine is now 3 phases: ACTIVE, IDLE, ENDED
- `active_committed` in persisted state normalizes to ACTIVE (not IDLE) so pending finalization isn't lost on upgrade

**PostCommit carry-forward**
- After condensation, uncommitted files are carried forward to a new shadow branch
- Ensures the next commit gets its own checkpoint ID instead of accumulating into the previous one

**Bug fixes from review feedback**
- `condenseAndUpdateState` now returns `bool` — prevents phantom checkpoint IDs when condensation fails
- Auto-commit now plumbs `TurnID` through to `WriteCommittedOptions` (was dead data)
- Auto-commit clears `TurnCheckpointIDs` on re-prompt

**Documentation updates**
- Removed stale "Approach B" (commit message search) from bidirectional lookup docs — CLI always reads from tree at HEAD
- Fixed stale `PendingCheckpointID` reference in KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md
- Updated `LastCheckpointID` comment to reflect 1:1 model

### What doesn't change

- User's branch history is untouched — the only addition to user commits is the single `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer
- Shadow branch lifecycle is unchanged
- `entire/checkpoints/v1` tree structure is unchanged — same sharded folder layout
- The CLI reads checkpoints from tree at HEAD, not from commit messages

> AGENT

The key is at line 530-544. Here's how it works:

**PostCommit iterates over all sessions for this worktree** (line 530), not just the "matching" one. Each session carries its own `FilesTouched` list and `BaseCommit`.

The matching happens through two mechanisms:

1. **`state.FilesTouched`** — The `SaveChanges` hook (called on every agent file write) appends files to the session's `FilesTouched` list. So any session that's been actively writing files has a non-empty list.

2. **The state machine transition** — `ACTIVE + GitCommit` emits `ActionCondense`, which always fires condensation if there's new transcript content (`hasNew`). It doesn't check whether the committed files overlap with `FilesTouched`. It condenses the session because the session is active and the agent is still working.

So the answer to your question: **it doesn't check file overlap at all for ACTIVE sessions.** If the session is ACTIVE (agent is mid-turn) and there's new transcript content, every commit triggers condensation for that session. The assumption is: if the agent is active and a commit happens, it's the agent's work.

The `FilesTouched` check only matters for `ENDED` sessions (`ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched`) — those need proof that the session actually touched files before condensing on a post-session commit.

After condensation, `FilesTouched` is cleared, `BaseCommit` advances to the new HEAD, and carry-forward moves any uncommitted files to a fresh shadow branch. When the agent writes more files, `FilesTouched` builds back up, and the next commit repeats the cycle with a new checkpoint ID.

> AGENT

Ah, I see — the **user commits manually between prompts** (session is IDLE), and they split the changes across two commits.

Let me trace through that:

1. Agent finishes turn → session goes IDLE, `FilesTouched = [A, B, C]`
2. User commits files A, B → PostCommit fires
3. Session is IDLE, `IDLE + GitCommit` emits `ActionCondense`
4. Condensation happens with checkpoint ID `abc...`, transcript is complete (turn is over)
5. Carry-forward **doesn't fire** — that's gated on `state.Phase.IsActive()`, and the session is IDLE
6. `FilesTouched` is cleared to `nil` by condensation
7. User commits file C → PostCommit fires
8. Session is IDLE, `IDLE + GitCommit` emits `ActionCondense`
9. `hasNew` check: `sessionHasNewContent` compares transcript against `CheckpointTranscriptStart` — **no new content** since the agent hasn't done anything
10. Falls to the `else` branch → just updates `BaseCommit`, no condensation

So file C's commit gets **no checkpoint at all**. The trailer from PrepareCommitMsg would use `LastCheckpointID` (set during step 4) to add the same `abc...` trailer, but there's no second checkpoint folder on `entire/checkpoints/v1`.

That's the old 1:N behavior leaking through. In the 1:1 model, this second commit should get its own checkpoint ID with the same transcript data. The carry-forward logic only runs for ACTIVE sessions — IDLE sessions with remaining files aren't handled.

Want me to fix this? The fix would be: after condensation for IDLE/ENDED sessions, check for remaining uncommitted files in the same way we do for ACTIVE sessions, and if there are any, ensure the next commit gets its own checkpoint rather than reusing `LastCheckpointID`.

> AGENT

It only commits `test.txt`. The session touched `A.txt, B.txt` in round 1. Since `commitWithCheckpointTrailer` only commits `test.txt`, the `committedFileSet` won't include `A.txt` or `B.txt`. So carry-forward will find `remaining = [A.txt, B.txt]` and set `state.FilesTouched = [A.txt, B.txt]`.

Then in round 2, `SaveChanges` adds `C.txt, D.txt` to `FilesTouched`, resulting in `[A.txt, B.txt, C.txt, D.txt]`. That's why the test fails.

The test was designed for the old behavior where carry-forward only ran for ACTIVE sessions. The test uses IDLE sessions. The fix: the test needs to include the session's files in the commit. Let me look at what files the test committed in round 1 more carefully:

All green. The fix:

1. **Carry-forward now runs for all phases** (not just ACTIVE) — when a user splits their commit across two `git commit` invocations, each gets its own checkpoint ID
2. `carryForwardToNewShadowBranch` already resets `CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0` and clears `LastCheckpointID`, so the second commit correctly writes the full transcript under a fresh checkpoint ID
3. Updated the test to commit the session's actual files (`A.txt, B.txt` then `C.txt, D.txt`) instead of an unrelated `test.txt`

> DEVELOPER

how do we determine this is a follow up commit and not something completely new

> AGENT

Good question. Right now, after carry-forward for an IDLE session, we don't properly distinguish them.

Here's the problem: carry-forward resets `CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0` and creates a shadow branch with the remaining files. When the next commit happens:

1. `sessionHasNewContent` finds the shadow branch, compares transcript lines against `CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0` → `hasNew = true`
2. Condensation fires regardless of what files are actually in the commit

So if the user commits an unrelated `README.md` edit, it still triggers condensation for the carried-forward session — giving an unrelated commit a checkpoint trailer and session data it shouldn't have.

The overlap check in `sessionHasNewContentFromLiveTranscript` (staged files vs modified files) was designed to prevent this, but it's only used when **no shadow branch exists**. After carry-forward creates a shadow branch, that check is bypassed.

The fix should be: when `hasNew` comes from a carry-forward shadow branch (not from actual new transcript content), we should also check that the committed files overlap with `state.FilesTouched`. Something like:

```go
case session.ActionCondense:
    if hasNew && (hasNewTranscript || hasOverlappingFiles(committedFileSet, state.FilesTouched)) {
```

so we know the last active session was idle but got at least one commit that was partial, now we have the shadowbranch with still a diff. on the next commit we could compare if the files being commited have an overlap with the diff, right?

> AGENT

Right. The shadow branch after carry-forward contains exactly the remaining uncommitted files. We can compare the committed files against what's in the shadow branch diff — if there's overlap, it's a follow-up commit for this session. If not, it's unrelated.

Actually, we already have that information without reading the shadow branch diff: `state.FilesTouched` is set to the remaining files by carry-forward (line 1549: `state.FilesTouched = remainingFiles`). So we just check if the committed files overlap with `state.FilesTouched`.

    24→// an ACTIVE session condenses immediately and stays ACTIVE.

    32→

    37→	setupSessionWithCheckpoint(t, s, repo, dir, sessionID)

   179→func TestPostCommit_ShadowBranch_PreservedWhenUncondensedActiveSessionExists(t *testing.T) {

   184→	require.NoError(t, err)
   185→

   187→	idleSessionID := "test-postcommit-idle-multi"
   188→	activeSessionID := "test-postcommit-active-multi"

   202→	idleState.LastInteractionTime = nil
   203→	require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(idleState))
   204→
   205→	// Create a second session with the SAME base commit and worktree (concurrent session).
   206→	// This session is ACTIVE but has NO checkpoints (StepCount=0, no shadow branch content).
   207→	// Because it has no new content, it will NOT be condensed, and its shadow branch must
   208→	// be preserved so it can save checkpoints later.
   209→	now := time.Now()

   217→		LastInteractionTime: &now,

   219→	}
   220→	require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(activeState))
   221→
   222→	// Record shadow branch name before PostCommit

   225→	// Create a commit WITH the checkpoint trailer

   228→	// Run PostCommit
   229→	err = s.PostCommit()
   230→	require.NoError(t, err)
   231→
   232→	// Verify the ACTIVE session stays ACTIVE (immediate condensation model)
   233→	activeState, err = s.loadSessionState(activeSessionID)
   234→	require.NoError(t, err)
   235→	assert.Equal(t, session.PhaseActive, activeState.Phase,
   236→		"ACTIVE session should stay ACTIVE after GitCommit")
   237→
   238→	// Verify the IDLE session actually condensed (entire/checkpoints/v1 branch should exist)
   239→	idleState, err = s.loadSessionState(idleSessionID)
   240→	require.NoError(t, err)
   241→	sessionsRef, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName), true)
   242→	require.NoError(t, err, "entire/checkpoints/v1 branch should exist after IDLE session condensation")
   243→	require.NotNil(t, sessionsRef)
   244→
   245→	// Verify IDLE session's StepCount was reset by condensation
   246→	assert.Equal(t, 0, idleState.StepCount,

   248→
   249→	// Verify shadow branch is preserved because the ACTIVE session was not condensed

   251→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranch)
   252→	_, err = repo.Reference(refName, true)

   485→	state, err = s.loadSessionState(sessionID)
   486→	require.NoError(t, err)
   487→	assert.Equal(t, newHeadHash, state.BaseCommit,
   488→		"BaseCommit should be updated to new HEAD via fallthrough")
   489→
   490→	// StepCount unchanged
   491→	assert.Equal(t, originalStepCount, state.StepCount,
   492→		"StepCount should be unchanged when no condensation happened")
   493→}

   495→// TestPostCommit_EndedSession_NoFilesTouched_Discards verifies that an ENDED
   496→// session with no files touched takes the discard path, updating BaseCommit.
   497→func TestPostCommit_EndedSession_NoFilesTouched_Discards(t *testing.T) {

   514→	state.Phase = session.PhaseEnded
   515→	state.EndedAt = &now
   516→	state.FilesTouched = nil // No files touched
   517→	require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(state))

   519→	// Record original StepCount
   520→	originalStepCount := state.StepCount
   521→
   522→	// Create a commit with the checkpoint trailer

   524→
   525→	// Get new HEAD hash

   530→	// Run PostCommit

   536→	require.Error(t, err,

   538→
   539→	// BaseCommit should be updated to new HEAD
   540→	state, err = s.loadSessionState(sessionID)

   554→// TestPostCommit_CondensationFailure_EndedSession_PreservesShadowBranch verifies
   555→// that when condensation fails for an ENDED session with files touched,
   556→// BaseCommit is preserved (not updated).
   557→func TestPostCommit_CondensationFailure_EndedSession_PreservesShadowBranch(t *testing.T) {
   558→	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
   559→	t.Chdir(dir)
   560→
   561→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
   562→	require.NoError(t, err)
   563→
   564→	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
   565→	sessionID := "test-postcommit-condense-fail-ended"
   566→
   567→	// Initialize session and save a checkpoint
   568→	setupSessionWithCheckpoint(t, s, repo, dir, sessionID)
   569→
   570→	// Set phase to ENDED with files touched
   571→	state, err := s.loadSessionState(sessionID)
   572→	require.NoError(t, err)
   573→	now := time.Now()
   574→	state.Phase = session.PhaseEnded
   575→	state.EndedAt = &now
   576→	state.FilesTouched = []string{"test.txt"}
   577→	require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(state))
   578→
   579→	// Record original BaseCommit and StepCount
   580→	originalBaseCommit := state.BaseCommit
   581→	originalStepCount := state.StepCount
   582→
   583→	// Corrupt shadow branch by pointing it at ZeroHash
   584→	shadowBranch := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   585→	corruptRef := plumbing.NewHashReference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranch), plumbing.ZeroHash)
   586→	require.NoError(t, repo.Storer.SetReference(corruptRef))
   587→
   588→	// Create a commit with the checkpoint trailer
   589→	commitWithCheckpointTrailer(t, repo, dir, "e5f6a1b2c3d5")
   590→
   591→	// Run PostCommit
   592→	err = s.PostCommit()
   593→	require.NoError(t, err, "PostCommit should not return error even when condensation fails")
   594→
   595→	// Verify BaseCommit was NOT updated (condensation failed)
   596→	state, err = s.loadSessionState(sessionID)
   597→	require.NoError(t, err)
   598→	assert.Equal(t, originalBaseCommit, state.BaseCommit,
   599→		"BaseCommit should NOT be updated when condensation fails for ENDED session")
   600→	assert.Equal(t, originalStepCount, state.StepCount,
   601→		"StepCount should NOT be reset when condensation fails for ENDED session")
   602→
   603→	// Verify entire/checkpoints/v1 branch does NOT exist (condensation failed)
   604→	_, err = repo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName), true)
   605→	require.Error(t, err,
   606→		"entire/checkpoints/v1 branch should NOT exist when condensation fails")
   607→
   608→	// Phase stays ENDED
   609→	assert.Equal(t, session.PhaseEnded, state.Phase,
   610→		"ENDED session should stay ENDED when condensation fails")
   611→}

   613→// TestTurnEnd_Active_NoActions verifies that HandleTurnEnd with no actions
   614→// is a no-op (normal ACTIVE → IDLE transition has no strategy-specific actions).
   615→func TestTurnEnd_Active_NoActions(t *testing.T) {
   616→	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
   617→	t.Chdir(dir)
   618→
   619→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
   620→	require.NoError(t, err)
   621→
   622→	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
   623→	sessionID := "test-turnend-no-actions"
   624→
   625→	// Initialize session and save a checkpoint
   626→	setupSessionWithCheckpoint(t, s, repo, dir, sessionID)
   627→
   628→	// Set phase to ACTIVE (normal turn, no commit during turn)
   629→	state, err := s.loadSessionState(sessionID)
   630→	require.NoError(t, err)
   631→	state.Phase = session.PhaseActive
   632→	require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(state))
   633→
   634→	originalBaseCommit := state.BaseCommit
   635→	originalStepCount := state.StepCount
   636→
   637→	// ACTIVE + TurnEnd → IDLE with no strategy-specific actions
   638→	result := session.Transition(state.Phase, session.EventTurnEnd, session.TransitionContext{})
   639→	remaining := session.ApplyCommonActions(state, result)
   640→
   641→	// Verify no strategy-specific actions for ACTIVE → IDLE
   642→	assert.Empty(t, remaining,
   643→		"ACTIVE + TurnEnd should not emit strategy-specific actions")
   644→
   645→	// Call HandleTurnEnd — should be a no-op (no TurnCheckpointIDs)
   646→	err = s.HandleTurnEnd(state)
   647→	require.NoError(t, err)
   648→
   649→	// Verify state is unchanged
   650→	assert.Equal(t, originalBaseCommit, state.BaseCommit,
   651→		"BaseCommit should be unchanged for no-op turn end")
   652→	assert.Equal(t, originalStepCount, state.StepCount,
   653→		"StepCount should be unchanged for no-op turn end")
   654→
   655→	// Shadow branch should still exist (not cleaned up)
   656→	shadowBranch := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(originalBaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   657→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranch)
   658→	_, err = repo.Reference(refName, true)
   659→	assert.NoError(t, err,
   660→		"shadow branch should still exist after no-op turn end")
   661→}

   663→// TestPostCommit_FilesTouched_ResetsAfterCondensation verifies that FilesTouched
   664→// is reset after condensation, so subsequent condensations only contain the files
   665→// touched since the last commit — not the accumulated history.
   666→func TestPostCommit_FilesTouched_ResetsAfterCondensation(t *testing.T) {
   667→	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
   668→	t.Chdir(dir)
   669→
   670→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
   671→	require.NoError(t, err)
   672→
   673→	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
   674→	sessionID := "test-filestouched-reset"
   675→
   676→	// --- Round 1: Save checkpoint touching files A.txt and B.txt ---
   677→
   678→	metadataDir := ".entire/metadata/" + sessionID
   679→	metadataDirAbs := filepath.Join(dir, metadataDir)
   680→	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(metadataDirAbs, 0o755))
   681→
   682→	transcript := `{"type":"human","message":{"content":"round 1 prompt"}}
   683→{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":"round 1 response"}}
   684→`
   685→	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(
   686→		filepath.Join(metadataDirAbs, paths.TranscriptFileName),
   687→		[]byte(transcript), 0o644))
   688→
   689→	// Create files A.txt and B.txt
   690→	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "A.txt"), []byte("file A"), 0o644))
   691→	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "B.txt"), []byte("file B"), 0o644))
   692→
   693→	err = s.SaveChanges(SaveContext{
   694→		SessionID:      sessionID,
   695→		ModifiedFiles:  []string{},
   696→		NewFiles:       []string{"A.txt", "B.txt"},
   697→		DeletedFiles:   []string{},
   698→		MetadataDir:    metadataDir,
   699→		MetadataDirAbs: metadataDirAbs,
   700→		CommitMessage:  "Checkpoint 1: files A and B",
   701→		AuthorName:     "Test",
   702→		AuthorEmail:    "test@test.com",
   703→	})
   704→	require.NoError(t, err)
   705→
   706→	// Set phase to IDLE so PostCommit triggers immediate condensation
   707→	state, err := s.loadSessionState(sessionID)
   708→	require.NoError(t, err)
   709→	state.Phase = session.PhaseIdle
   710→	require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(state))
   711→
   712→	// Verify FilesTouched has A.txt and B.txt before condensation
   713→	assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{"A.txt", "B.txt"}, state.FilesTouched,
   714→		"FilesTouched should contain A.txt and B.txt before first condensation")
   715→
   716→	// --- Commit A.txt, B.txt and condense (round 1) ---
   717→	checkpointID1 := "a1a2a3a4a5a6"
   718→	commitFilesWithTrailer(t, repo, dir, checkpointID1, "A.txt", "B.txt")
   719→
   720→	err = s.PostCommit()
   721→	require.NoError(t, err)
   722→
   723→	// Verify condensation happened
   724→	_, err = repo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName), true)
   725→	require.NoError(t, err, "entire/checkpoints/v1 should exist after first condensation")
   726→
   727→	// Verify first condensation contains A.txt and B.txt
   728→	store := checkpoint.NewGitStore(repo)
   729→	cpID1 := id.MustCheckpointID(checkpointID1)
   730→	summary1, err := store.ReadCommitted(context.Background(), cpID1)
   731→	require.NoError(t, err)
   732→	require.NotNil(t, summary1)
   733→	assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{"A.txt", "B.txt"}, summary1.FilesTouched,
   734→		"First condensation should contain A.txt and B.txt")
   735→
   736→	// Verify FilesTouched was reset after condensation
   737→	state, err = s.loadSessionState(sessionID)
   738→	require.NoError(t, err)
   739→	assert.Nil(t, state.FilesTouched,
   740→		"FilesTouched should be nil after condensation (all files were committed)")
   741→
   742→	// --- Round 2: Save checkpoint touching files C.txt and D.txt ---
   743→
   744→	// Append to transcript for round 2
   745→	transcript2 := `{"type":"human","message":{"content":"round 2 prompt"}}
   746→{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":"round 2 response"}}
   747→`
   748→	f, err := os.OpenFile(
   749→		filepath.Join(metadataDirAbs, paths.TranscriptFileName),
   750→		os.O_APPEND|os.O_WRONLY, 0o644)
   751→	require.NoError(t, err)
   752→	_, err = f.WriteString(transcript2)
   753→	require.NoError(t, err)
   754→	require.NoError(t, f.Close())
   755→
   756→	// Create files C.txt and D.txt
   757→	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "C.txt"), []byte("file C"), 0o644))
   758→	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "D.txt"), []byte("file D"), 0o644))
   759→
   760→	err = s.SaveChanges(SaveContext{
   761→		SessionID:      sessionID,
   762→		ModifiedFiles:  []string{},
   763→		NewFiles:       []string{"C.txt", "D.txt"},
   764→		DeletedFiles:   []string{},
   765→		MetadataDir:    metadataDir,
   766→		MetadataDirAbs: metadataDirAbs,
   767→		CommitMessage:  "Checkpoint 2: files C and D",
   768→		AuthorName:     "Test",
   769→		AuthorEmail:    "test@test.com",
   770→	})
   771→	require.NoError(t, err)
   772→
   773→	// Set phase to IDLE for immediate condensation
   774→	state, err = s.loadSessionState(sessionID)
   775→	require.NoError(t, err)
   776→	state.Phase = session.PhaseIdle
   777→	require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(state))
   778→
   779→	// Verify FilesTouched only has C.txt and D.txt (NOT A.txt, B.txt)
   780→	assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{"C.txt", "D.txt"}, state.FilesTouched,
   781→		"FilesTouched should only contain C.txt and D.txt after reset")
   782→
   783→	// --- Commit C.txt, D.txt and condense (round 2) ---
   784→	checkpointID2 := "b1b2b3b4b5b6"
   785→	commitFilesWithTrailer(t, repo, dir, checkpointID2, "C.txt", "D.txt")
   786→
   787→	err = s.PostCommit()
   788→	require.NoError(t, err)
   789→
   790→	// Verify second condensation contains ONLY C.txt and D.txt
   791→	cpID2 := id.MustCheckpointID(checkpointID2)
   792→	summary2, err := store.ReadCommitted(context.Background(), cpID2)
   793→	require.NoError(t, err)
   794→	require.NotNil(t, summary2, "Second condensation should exist")
   795→	assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{"C.txt", "D.txt"}, summary2.FilesTouched,
   796→		"Second condensation should only contain C.txt and D.txt, not accumulated files from first condensation")
   797→}

   799→// TestSubtractFiles verifies that subtractFiles correctly removes files present
   800→// in the exclude set and preserves files not in it.
   801→func TestSubtractFiles(t *testing.T) {
   802→	t.Parallel()
   803→
   804→	tests := []struct {
   805→		name     string
   806→		files    []string
   807→		exclude  map[string]struct{}
   808→		expected []string
   809→	}{
   810→		{
   811→			name:     "no overlap",
   812→			files:    []string{"a.txt", "b.txt"},
   813→			exclude:  map[string]struct{}{"c.txt": {}},
   814→			expected: []string{"a.txt", "b.txt"},
   815→		},
   816→		{
   817→			name:     "full overlap",
   818→			files:    []string{"a.txt", "b.txt"},
   819→			exclude:  map[string]struct{}{"a.txt": {}, "b.txt": {}},
   820→			expected: nil,
   821→		},
   822→		{
   823→			name:     "partial overlap",
   824→			files:    []string{"a.txt", "b.txt", "c.txt"},
   825→			exclude:  map[string]struct{}{"b.txt": {}},
   826→			expected: []string{"a.txt", "c.txt"},
   827→		},
   828→		{
   829→			name:     "empty files",
   830→			files:    []string{},
   831→			exclude:  map[string]struct{}{"a.txt": {}},
   832→			expected: nil,
   833→		},
   834→		{
   835→			name:     "empty exclude",
   836→			files:    []string{"a.txt", "b.txt"},
   837→			exclude:  map[string]struct{}{},
   838→			expected: []string{"a.txt", "b.txt"},
   839→		},
   840→	}
   841→
   842→	for _, tt := range tests {
   843→		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
   844→			t.Parallel()
   845→			result := subtractFiles(tt.files, tt.exclude)
   846→			assert.Equal(t, tt.expected, result)
   847→		})
   848→	}
   849→}

   851→// TestFilesChangedInCommit verifies that filesChangedInCommit correctly extracts
   852→// the set of files changed in a commit by diffing against its parent.
   853→func TestFilesChangedInCommit(t *testing.T) {
   854→	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
   855→	t.Chdir(dir)
   856→
   857→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
   858→	require.NoError(t, err)
   859→
   860→	wt, err := repo.Worktree()
   861→	require.NoError(t, err)
   862→
   863→	// Create files and commit them
   864→	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "file1.txt"), []byte("content1"), 0o644))
   865→	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "file2.txt"), []byte("content2"), 0o644))
   866→	_, err = wt.Add("file1.txt")
   867→	require.NoError(t, err)
   868→	_, err = wt.Add("file2.txt")
   869→	require.NoError(t, err)
   870→
   871→	commitHash, err := wt.Commit("add files", &git.CommitOptions{
   872→		Author: &object.Signature{Name: "Test", Email: "test@test.com", When: time.Now()},
   873→	})
   874→	require.NoError(t, err)
   875→
   876→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(commitHash)
   877→	require.NoError(t, err)
   878→
   879→	changed := filesChangedInCommit(commit)
   880→	assert.Contains(t, changed, "file1.txt")
   881→	assert.Contains(t, changed, "file2.txt")
   882→	// test.txt was in the initial commit, not this one
   883→	assert.NotContains(t, changed, "test.txt")
   884→}

   921→// TestPostCommit_ActiveSession_CarryForward_PartialCommit verifies that when an
   922→// ACTIVE session has touched files A, B, C but only A and B are committed, the
   923→// remaining file C is carried forward to a new shadow branch.
   924→func TestPostCommit_ActiveSession_CarryForward_PartialCommit(t *testing.T) {
   925→	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
   926→	t.Chdir(dir)
   927→
   928→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
   929→	require.NoError(t, err)
   930→
   931→	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
   932→	sessionID := "test-carry-forward-partial"
   933→
   934→	// Create metadata directory with transcript
   935→	metadataDir := ".entire/metadata/" + sessionID
   936→	metadataDirAbs := filepath.Join(dir, metadataDir)
   937→	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(metadataDirAbs, 0o755))
   938→
   939→	transcript := `{"type":"human","message":{"content":"create files A B C"}}
   940→{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":"creating files"}}
   941→`
   942→	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(
   943→		filepath.Join(metadataDirAbs, paths.TranscriptFileName),
   944→		[]byte(transcript), 0o644))
   945→
   946→	// Create all three files
   947→	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "A.txt"), []byte("file A"), 0o644))
   948→	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "B.txt"), []byte("file B"), 0o644))
   949→	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "C.txt"), []byte("file C"), 0o644))
   950→
   951→	// Save checkpoint with all three files
   952→	err = s.SaveChanges(SaveContext{
   953→		SessionID:      sessionID,
   954→		ModifiedFiles:  []string{},
   955→		NewFiles:       []string{"A.txt", "B.txt", "C.txt"},
   956→		DeletedFiles:   []string{},
   957→		MetadataDir:    metadataDir,
   958→		MetadataDirAbs: metadataDirAbs,
   959→		CommitMessage:  "Checkpoint: files A, B, C",
   960→		AuthorName:     "Test",
   961→		AuthorEmail:    "test@test.com",
   962→	})
   963→	require.NoError(t, err)
   964→
   965→	// Set phase to ACTIVE (agent mid-turn)
   966→	state, err := s.loadSessionState(sessionID)
   967→	require.NoError(t, err)
   968→	state.Phase = session.PhaseActive
   969→	require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(state))
   970→
   971→	// Verify FilesTouched contains all three files
   972→	assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{"A.txt", "B.txt", "C.txt"}, state.FilesTouched)
   973→
   974→	// Commit ONLY A.txt and B.txt (not C.txt) with checkpoint trailer
   975→	wt, err := repo.Worktree()
   976→	require.NoError(t, err)
   977→	_, err = wt.Add("A.txt")
   978→	require.NoError(t, err)
   979→	_, err = wt.Add("B.txt")
   980→	require.NoError(t, err)
   981→
   982→	cpID := "cf1cf2cf3cf4"
   983→	commitMsg := "commit A and B\n\n" + trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ": " + cpID + "\n"
   984→	_, err = wt.Commit(commitMsg, &git.CommitOptions{
