   212→// TestShadow_AmendPreservesTrailer tests that `git commit --amend` preserves
   213→// the checkpoint trailer from the original commit.
   214→//
   215→// When a user amends a commit that has an Entire-Checkpoint trailer, the
   216→// prepare-commit-msg hook (called with source="commit") should preserve the
   217→// existing trailer. No duplicate condensation should occur.
   218→//
   219→// Hook behavior tested:
   220→//   - prepare-commit-msg with source="commit": preserves existing trailer
   221→//   - post-commit after amend: no duplicate condensation
   222→func TestShadow_AmendPreservesTrailer(t *testing.T) {
   223→	t.Parallel()
   224→
   225→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, strategy.StrategyNameManualCommit)
   226→
   227→	// ========================================
   228→	// Phase 1: Full workflow - create checkpoint and commit
   229→	// ========================================
   230→	t.Log("Phase 1: Create session, checkpoint, and commit")
   231→
   232→	sess := env.NewSession()
   233→	if err := env.SimulateUserPromptSubmit(sess.ID); err != nil {
   234→		t.Fatalf("SimulateUserPromptSubmit failed: %v", err)
   235→	}
   236→
   237→	// Create a file and checkpoint
   238→	env.WriteFile("main.go", "package main\n\nfunc main() {}\n")
   239→	sess.CreateTranscript("Create main.go", []FileChange{
   240→		{Path: "main.go", Content: "package main\n\nfunc main() {}\n"},
   241→	})
   242→	if err := env.SimulateStop(sess.ID, sess.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
   243→		t.Fatalf("SimulateStop failed: %v", err)
   244→	}
   245→
   246→	// Commit with hooks (triggers condensation)
   247→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Initial implementation", "main.go")
   248→
   249→	originalCommitHash := env.GetHeadHash()
   250→	originalCheckpointID := env.GetCheckpointIDFromCommitMessage(originalCommitHash)
   251→	if originalCheckpointID == "" {
   252→		t.Fatal("Original commit should have a checkpoint trailer")
   253→	}
   254→	t.Logf("Original commit %s has checkpoint ID: %s", originalCommitHash[:7], originalCheckpointID)
   255→
   256→	// Verify condensation happened
   257→	if !env.BranchExists(paths.MetadataBranchName) {
   258→		t.Fatal("entire/checkpoints/v1 branch should exist after condensation")
   259→	}
   260→
   261→	// Record the sessions branch state for later comparison
   262→	sessionsCommitBefore := env.GetLatestCommitMessageOnBranch(paths.MetadataBranchName)
   263→	t.Logf("Sessions branch commit before amend:\n%s", sessionsCommitBefore)
   264→
   265→	// ========================================
   266→	// Phase 2: Amend the commit
   267→	// ========================================
   268→	t.Log("Phase 2: Amend the commit")
   269→
   270→	// Amend with the same message (simulating a minor message edit or staging additional files)
   271→	env.GitCommitAmendWithShadowHooks("Initial implementation (amended)")
   272→
   273→	amendedCommitHash := env.GetHeadHash()
   274→	t.Logf("Amended commit: %s", amendedCommitHash[:7])
   275→
   276→	// The amended commit hash should be different from the original
   277→	if amendedCommitHash == originalCommitHash {
   278→		t.Error("Amended commit should have a different hash")
   279→	}
   280→
   281→	// ========================================
   282→	// Phase 3: Verify trailer is preserved
   283→	// ========================================
   284→	t.Log("Phase 3: Verify checkpoint trailer is preserved")
   285→
   286→	amendedCheckpointID := env.GetCheckpointIDFromCommitMessage(amendedCommitHash)
   287→	if amendedCheckpointID == "" {
   288→		t.Fatal("Amended commit should still have a checkpoint trailer")
   289→	}
   290→	t.Logf("Amended commit has checkpoint ID: %s", amendedCheckpointID)
   291→
   292→	// The checkpoint ID should be the SAME as the original
   293→	if amendedCheckpointID != originalCheckpointID {
   294→		t.Errorf("Amended commit should preserve original checkpoint ID.\nOriginal: %s\nAmended:  %s",
   295→			originalCheckpointID, amendedCheckpointID)
   296→	}
   297→
   298→	// ========================================
   299→	// Phase 4: Verify no duplicate condensation
   300→	// ========================================
   301→	t.Log("Phase 4: Verify no duplicate condensation")
   302→
   303→	// The sessions branch commit should not have changed (no new condensation)
   304→	sessionsCommitAfter := env.GetLatestCommitMessageOnBranch(paths.MetadataBranchName)
   305→	if sessionsCommitBefore != sessionsCommitAfter {
   306→		t.Logf("Sessions branch commit changed after amend:\nBefore:\n%s\nAfter:\n%s",
   307→			sessionsCommitBefore, sessionsCommitAfter)
   308→		// This is not necessarily an error -- post-commit might trigger condensation
   309→		// if there's new content. But with no new session activity, it should be the same.
   310→		t.Log("Note: sessions branch was updated (may indicate duplicate condensation)")
   311→	} else {
   312→		t.Log("Sessions branch unchanged after amend (no duplicate condensation)")
   313→	}
   314→
   315→	// Verify the checkpoint data still exists and is accessible
   316→	summaryPath := CheckpointSummaryPath(originalCheckpointID)
   317→	if !env.FileExistsInBranch(paths.MetadataBranchName, summaryPath) {
   318→		t.Errorf("Checkpoint metadata should still exist at %s after amend", summaryPath)
   319→	}
   320→
   321→	transcriptPath := SessionFilePath(originalCheckpointID, paths.TranscriptFileName)
   322→	if !env.FileExistsInBranch(paths.MetadataBranchName, transcriptPath) {
   323→		t.Errorf("Transcript should still exist at %s after amend", transcriptPath)
   324→	}
   325→
   326→	t.Log("AmendPreservesTrailer test completed successfully")
   327→}

## Existing Integration Test Coverage

**Well covered:**
- Basic 1:1 checkpoint-to-commit flow (`last_checkpoint_id_test.go`)

- Agent commit always gets trailer
- Unrelated file commits don't get trailer
- Full workflow with rewind and condensation (`manual_commit_workflow_test.go`)
- Phase transitions: ACTIVE → IDLE on stop, ACTIVE stays ACTIVE on commit (`phase_transitions_test.go`)
- Trailer removal skips condensation (opt-out)
- Amend preserves trailer
- LastCheckpointID cleared on new prompt
- Shadow branch cleanup and migration

## Missing Integration Tests for New Complex Flows

**Not covered:**

1. **Deferred transcript finalization** - `TestShadow_CommitBeforeStop` tests mid-turn commits but doesn't verify that `HandleTurnEnd` replaces the provisional transcript with the full transcript via `UpdateCommitted`. This is a core part of the new model.

2. **Carry-forward for partial commits (ACTIVE)** - Unit tests exist in `phase_postcommit_test.go` but no integration test verifies the full flow: commit some files → remaining files carried forward → next commit gets own checkpoint ID.

3. **Carry-forward for partial commits (IDLE)** - The scenario we just fixed. IDLE session with files A+B, user commits A → B gets carry-forward → next commit with B gets its own checkpoint.

4. **Multiple commits in same ACTIVE turn with finalization** - When user makes 2+ commits during one agent turn, each should get its own checkpoint ID, all stored in `TurnCheckpointIDs`, and all finalized with full transcript at turn end.

5. **Overlap check for non-ACTIVE sessions** - After carry-forward, an unrelated commit (files not in session's `FilesTouched`) should NOT get the session's checkpoint trailer.

   639→type RewindPoint struct {
   640→	ID               string
   641→	Message          string
   642→	MetadataDir      string

   644→	IsTaskCheckpoint bool
   645→	ToolUseID        string

   650→// GetRewindPoints returns available rewind points using the CLI.
   651→func (env *TestEnv) GetRewindPoints() []RewindPoint {
   652→	env.T.Helper()
   653→
   654→	// Run rewind --list using the shared binary
   655→	cmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "rewind", "--list")
   656→	cmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
   657→	cmd.Env = env.cliEnv()
   658→
   659→	output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
   660→	if err != nil {
   661→		env.T.Fatalf("rewind --list failed: %v\nOutput: %s", err, output)
   662→	}
   663→
   664→	// Parse JSON output
   665→	var jsonPoints []struct {
   666→		ID               string `json:"id"`
   667→		Message          string `json:"message"`
   668→		MetadataDir      string `json:"metadata_dir"`
   669→		Date             string `json:"date"`
   670→		IsTaskCheckpoint bool   `json:"is_task_checkpoint"`
   671→		ToolUseID        string `json:"tool_use_id"`
   672→		IsLogsOnly       bool   `json:"is_logs_only"`
   673→		CondensationID   string `json:"condensation_id"`
   674→	}
   675→
   676→	if err := json.Unmarshal(output, &jsonPoints); err != nil {
   677→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to parse rewind points: %v\nOutput: %s", err, output)
   678→	}
   679→
   680→	points := make([]RewindPoint, len(jsonPoints))
   681→	for i, jp := range jsonPoints {
   682→		date, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, jp.Date)
   683→		points[i] = RewindPoint{
   684→			ID:               jp.ID,
   685→			Message:          jp.Message,
   686→			MetadataDir:      jp.MetadataDir,
   687→			Date:             date,
   688→			IsTaskCheckpoint: jp.IsTaskCheckpoint,
   689→			ToolUseID:        jp.ToolUseID,
   690→			IsLogsOnly:       jp.IsLogsOnly,
   691→			CondensationID:   jp.CondensationID,
   692→		}
   693→	}
   694→
   695→	return points
   696→}

   797→// FileExistsInBranch checks if a file exists in a specific branch's tree.
   798→func (env *TestEnv) FileExistsInBranch(branchName, filePath string) bool {
   799→	env.T.Helper()
   800→
   801→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
   802→	if err != nil {
   803→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)
   804→	}
   805→
   806→	// Get the branch reference
   807→	ref, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(branchName), true)
   808→	if err != nil {
   809→		// Try as a remote-style ref
   810→		ref, err = repo.Reference(plumbing.ReferenceName("refs/heads/"+branchName), true)
   811→		if err != nil {
   812→			return false
   813→		}
   814→	}
   815→
   816→	// Get the commit
   817→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   818→	if err != nil {
   819→		return false
   820→	}
   821→
   822→	// Get the tree
   823→	tree, err := commit.Tree()
   824→	if err != nil {
   825→		return false
   826→	}
   827→
   828→	// Check if file exists
   829→	_, err = tree.File(filePath)
   830→	return err == nil
   831→}

   838→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)

   840→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)
   841→	}
   842→
   843→	// Get the branch reference
   844→	ref, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(branchName), true)
   845→	if err != nil {
   846→		// Try as a remote-style ref
   847→		ref, err = repo.Reference(plumbing.ReferenceName("refs/heads/"+branchName), true)
   848→		if err != nil {
   849→			return "", false
   850→		}
   851→	}
   852→
   853→	// Get the commit
   854→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   855→	if err != nil {
   856→		return "", false
   857→	}
   858→
   859→	// Get the tree

   861→	if err != nil {
   862→		return "", false

   864→
   865→	// Get the file

   869→	}
   870→
   871→	// Get the content
   872→	content, err := file.Contents()
   873→	if err != nil {

   877→	return content, true

   904→// GitCommitWithShadowHooks stages and commits files, simulating the prepare-commit-msg
   905→// and post-commit hooks as a human (with TTY). This is the default for tests.
   906→func (env *TestEnv) GitCommitWithShadowHooks(message string, files ...string) {
   907→	env.T.Helper()
   908→	env.gitCommitWithShadowHooks(message, true, files...)
   909→}
   910→
   911→// GitCommitWithShadowHooksAsAgent is like GitCommitWithShadowHooks but simulates
   912→// an agent commit (no TTY). This triggers the fast path in PrepareCommitMsg that
   913→// skips content detection and interactive prompts for ACTIVE sessions.
   914→func (env *TestEnv) GitCommitWithShadowHooksAsAgent(message string, files ...string) {
   915→	env.T.Helper()
   916→	env.gitCommitWithShadowHooks(message, false, files...)
   917→}
   918→
   919→// gitCommitWithShadowHooks is the shared implementation for committing with shadow hooks.
   920→// When simulateTTY is true, sets ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1 to simulate a human at the terminal.
   921→// When false, filters it out to simulate an agent subprocess (no controlling terminal).
   922→func (env *TestEnv) gitCommitWithShadowHooks(message string, simulateTTY bool, files ...string) {
   923→	env.T.Helper()
   924→
   925→	// Stage files using go-git
   926→	for _, file := range files {
   927→		env.GitAdd(file)
   928→	}
   929→
   930→	// Create a temp file for the commit message (prepare-commit-msg hook modifies this)
   931→	msgFile := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".git", "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
   932→	if err := os.WriteFile(msgFile, []byte(message), 0o644); err != nil {
   933→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to write commit message file: %v", err)
   934→	}
   935→
   936→	// Run prepare-commit-msg hook using the shared binary.
   937→	// Pass source="message" to match real `git commit -m` behavior.
   938→	prepCmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "git", "prepare-commit-msg", msgFile, "message")
   939→	prepCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
   940→	if simulateTTY {
   941→		// Simulate human at terminal: ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1 makes hasTTY() return true
   942→		// and askConfirmTTY() return defaultYes without reading from /dev/tty.
   943→		prepCmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1")
   944→	} else {
   945→		// Simulate agent: ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0 makes hasTTY() return false,
   946→		// triggering the fast path that adds trailers for ACTIVE sessions.
   947→		prepCmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0")
   948→	}
   949→	if output, err := prepCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
   950→		env.T.Logf("prepare-commit-msg output: %s", output)
   951→		// Don't fail - hook may silently succeed
   952→	}
   953→
   954→	// Read the modified message
   955→	modifiedMsg, err := os.ReadFile(msgFile)
   956→	if err != nil {
   957→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to read modified commit message: %v", err)
   958→	}
   959→
   960→	// Create the commit using go-git with the modified message
   961→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
   962→	if err != nil {
   963→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)
   964→	}
   965→
   966→	worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
   967→	if err != nil {
   968→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to get worktree: %v", err)
   969→	}
   970→
   971→	_, err = worktree.Commit(string(modifiedMsg), &git.CommitOptions{
   972→		Author: &object.Signature{
   973→			Name:  "Test User",
   974→			Email: "test@example.com",
   975→			When:  time.Now(),
   976→		},
   977→	})
   978→	if err != nil {
   979→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to commit: %v", err)
   980→	}
   981→
   982→	// Run post-commit hook using the shared binary
   983→	// This triggers condensation if the commit has an Entire-Checkpoint trailer
   984→	postCmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "git", "post-commit")
   985→	postCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
   986→	if output, err := postCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
   987→		env.T.Logf("post-commit output: %s", output)
   988→		// Don't fail - hook may silently succeed
   989→	}
   990→}
   991→
   992→// GitCommitAmendWithShadowHooks amends the last commit with shadow hooks.
   993→// This simulates `git commit --amend` with the prepare-commit-msg and post-commit hooks.
   994→// The prepare-commit-msg hook is called with "commit" source to indicate an amend.
   995→func (env *TestEnv) GitCommitAmendWithShadowHooks(message string, files ...string) {
   996→	env.T.Helper()
   997→
   998→	// Stage any additional files
   999→	for _, file := range files {
  1000→		env.GitAdd(file)
  1001→	}
  1002→
  1003→	// Write commit message to temp file
  1004→	msgFile := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".git", "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
  1005→	if err := os.WriteFile(msgFile, []byte(message), 0o644); err != nil {
  1006→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to write commit message file: %v", err)
  1007→	}
  1008→
  1009→	// Run prepare-commit-msg hook with "commit" source (indicates amend).
  1010→	// Set ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1 to simulate human (amend is always a human operation).

  1055→// GitCommitWithTrailerRemoved stages and commits files, simulating what happens when
  1056→// a user removes the Entire-Checkpoint trailer during commit message editing.
  1057→// This tests the opt-out behavior where removing the trailer skips condensation.
  1058→func (env *TestEnv) GitCommitWithTrailerRemoved(message string, files ...string) {
  1059→	env.T.Helper()
  1060→
  1061→	// Stage files using go-git
  1062→	for _, file := range files {
  1063→		env.GitAdd(file)
  1064→	}
  1065→
  1066→	// Create a temp file for the commit message (prepare-commit-msg hook modifies this)
  1067→	msgFile := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".git", "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
  1068→	if err := os.WriteFile(msgFile, []byte(message), 0o644); err != nil {
  1069→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to write commit message file: %v", err)
  1070→	}
  1071→
  1072→	// Run prepare-commit-msg hook using the shared binary.
  1073→	// Set ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1 to simulate human (this tests the editor flow where
  1074→	// the user removes the trailer before committing).
  1075→	prepCmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "git", "prepare-commit-msg", msgFile)
  1076→	prepCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
  1077→	prepCmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1")
  1078→	if output, err := prepCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
  1079→		env.T.Logf("prepare-commit-msg output: %s", output)
  1080→	}
  1081→
  1082→	// Read the modified message (with trailer added by hook)
  1083→	modifiedMsg, err := os.ReadFile(msgFile)
  1084→	if err != nil {
  1085→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to read modified commit message: %v", err)
  1086→	}
  1087→
  1088→	// REMOVE the Entire-Checkpoint trailer (simulating user editing the message)
  1089→	lines := strings.Split(string(modifiedMsg), "\n")
  1090→	var cleanedLines []string
  1091→	for _, line := range lines {
  1092→		// Skip the trailer and the comments about it
  1093→		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "Entire-Checkpoint:") {
  1094→			continue
  1095→		}
  1096→		if strings.Contains(line, "Remove the Entire-Checkpoint trailer") {
  1097→			continue
  1098→		}
  1099→		if strings.Contains(line, "trailer will be added to your next commit") {
  1100→			continue
  1101→		}
  1102→		cleanedLines = append(cleanedLines, line)
  1103→	}
  1104→	cleanedMsg := strings.TrimRight(strings.Join(cleanedLines, "\n"), "\n") + "\n"
  1105→
  1106→	// Create the commit using go-git with the cleaned message (no trailer)
  1107→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
  1108→	if err != nil {
  1109→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)
  1110→	}
  1111→
  1112→	worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
  1113→	if err != nil {
  1114→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to get worktree: %v", err)
  1115→	}
  1116→
  1117→	_, err = worktree.Commit(cleanedMsg, &git.CommitOptions{
  1118→		Author: &object.Signature{
  1119→			Name:  "Test User",
  1120→			Email: "test@example.com",
  1121→			When:  time.Now(),
  1122→		},
  1123→	})
  1124→	if err != nil {
  1125→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to commit: %v", err)
  1126→	}
  1127→
  1128→	// Run post-commit hook - since trailer was removed, no condensation should happen
  1129→	postCmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "git", "post-commit")
  1130→	postCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
  1131→	if output, err := postCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
  1132→		env.T.Logf("post-commit output: %s", output)
  1133→	}
  1134→}

  1162→// GetLatestCheckpointID returns the most recent checkpoint ID from the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch.
  1163→// This is used by tests that previously extracted the checkpoint ID from commit message trailers.

  1166→func (env *TestEnv) GetLatestCheckpointID() string {

  1188→	for _, line := range strings.Split(commit.Message, "\n") {
  1189→		line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
  1190→		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "Checkpoint: ") {
  1191→			return strings.TrimPrefix(line, "Checkpoint: ")

  1193→	}
  1194→
  1195→	env.T.Fatalf("could not find checkpoint ID in %s branch commit message:\n%s",
  1196→		paths.MetadataBranchName, commit.Message)
  1197→	return ""
  1198→}

  1253→// GetLatestCheckpointIDFromHistory walks backwards from HEAD on the active branch
  1254→// and returns the checkpoint ID from the first commit that has an Entire-Checkpoint trailer.
  1255→// This verifies that condensation actually happened (commit has trailer) without relying
  1256→// on timestamp-based matching.
  1257→func (env *TestEnv) GetLatestCheckpointIDFromHistory() string {
  1258→	env.T.Helper()
  1259→
  1260→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
  1261→	if err != nil {
  1262→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)
  1263→	}
  1264→
  1265→	head, err := repo.Head()
  1266→	if err != nil {
  1267→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to get HEAD: %v", err)
  1268→	}
  1269→
  1270→	commitIter, err := repo.Log(&git.LogOptions{From: head.Hash()})
  1271→	if err != nil {
  1272→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to iterate commits: %v", err)
  1273→	}
  1274→
  1275→	var checkpointID string
  1276→	//nolint:errcheck // ForEach callback handles errors
  1277→	commitIter.ForEach(func(c *object.Commit) error {
  1278→		if cpID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(c.Message); found {
  1279→			checkpointID = cpID.String()
  1280→			return errors.New("stop iteration") // Found it, stop
  1281→		}
  1282→		return nil
  1283→	})
  1284→
  1285→	if checkpointID == "" {
  1286→		env.T.Fatalf("no commit with Entire-Checkpoint trailer found in history")
  1287→	}
  1288→
  1289→	return checkpointID
  1290→}

  1316→func findModuleRoot() string {
  1317→	// Start from this source file's location and walk up to find go.mod
  1318→	_, thisFile, _, ok := runtime.Caller(0)
  1319→	if !ok {
  1320→		panic("failed to get current file path via runtime.Caller")
  1321→	}
  1322→	dir := filepath.Dir(thisFile)
  1323→
  1324→	for {
  1325→		if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, "go.mod")); err == nil {
  1326→			return dir
  1327→		}
  1328→		parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
  1329→		if parent == dir {
  1330→			panic("could not find go.mod starting from " + thisFile)
  1331→		}
  1332→		dir = parent
  1333→	}
  1334→}

   233→// CreateTranscript builds and writes a transcript for the session.

   235→	s.TranscriptBuilder.AddUserMessage(prompt)
   236→	s.TranscriptBuilder.AddAssistantMessage("I'll help you with that.")
   237→
   238→	for _, change := range changes {
   239→		toolID := s.TranscriptBuilder.AddToolUse("mcp__acp__Write", change.Path, change.Content)
   240→		s.TranscriptBuilder.AddToolResult(toolID)
   241→	}
   242→
   243→	s.TranscriptBuilder.AddAssistantMessage("Done!")
   244→
   245→	if err := s.TranscriptBuilder.WriteToFile(s.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
   246→		s.env.T.Fatalf("failed to write transcript: %v", err)
   247→	}
   248→
   249→	return s.TranscriptPath
   250→}

   478→func (r *GeminiHookRunner) runGeminiHookInRepoDir(hookName string, inputJSON []byte) error {
   479→	// Run using the shared test binary
   480→	// Command structure: entire hooks gemini <hook-name>
   481→	cmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "gemini", hookName)
   482→	cmd.Dir = r.RepoDir
   483→	cmd.Stdin = bytes.NewReader(inputJSON)
   484→	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
   485→		"ENTIRE_TEST_GEMINI_PROJECT_DIR="+r.GeminiProjectDir,
   486→	)
   487→
   488→	output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
   489→	if err != nil {
   490→		return fmt.Errorf("hook %s failed: %w\nInput: %s\nOutput: %s",
   491→			hookName, err, inputJSON, output)
   492→	}
   493→
   494→	r.T.Logf("Gemini hook %s output: %s", hookName, output)
   495→	return nil
   496→}

   615→// CreateGeminiTranscript creates a Gemini JSON transcript file for the session.
   616→func (s *GeminiSession) CreateGeminiTranscript(prompt string, changes []FileChange) string {
   617→	// Build Gemini-format transcript (JSON, not JSONL)
   618→	messages := []map[string]interface{}{
   619→		{
   620→			"type":    "user",
   621→			"content": prompt,
   622→		},
   623→		{
   624→			"type":    "assistant",
   625→			"content": "I'll help you with that.",
   626→		},
   627→	}
   628→
   629→	for _, change := range changes {
   630→		messages = append(messages, map[string]interface{}{
   631→			"type": "tool_use",
   632→			"name": "write_file",
   633→			"input": map[string]string{
   634→				"path":    change.Path,
   635→				"content": change.Content,
   636→			},
   637→		})
   638→		messages = append(messages, map[string]interface{}{
   639→			"type":   "tool_result",
   640→			"output": "File written successfully",
   641→		})
   642→	}
   643→
   644→	messages = append(messages, map[string]interface{}{
   645→		"type":    "assistant",
   646→		"content": "Done!",
   647→	})
   648→
   649→	transcript := map[string]interface{}{
   650→		"sessionId": s.ID,
   651→		"messages":  messages,
   652→	}
   653→
   654→	// Ensure directory exists
   655→	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(s.TranscriptPath), 0o755); err != nil {
   656→		s.env.T.Fatalf("failed to create transcript dir: %v", err)
   657→	}
   658→
   659→	// Write transcript
   660→	data, err := json.MarshalIndent(transcript, "", "  ")
   661→	if err != nil {
   662→		s.env.T.Fatalf("failed to marshal transcript: %v", err)
   663→	}
   664→	if err := os.WriteFile(s.TranscriptPath, data, 0o644); err != nil {
   665→		s.env.T.Fatalf("failed to write transcript: %v", err)
   666→	}
   667→
   668→	return s.TranscriptPath
   669→}

    54→		"transcript_path": "", // Not used for user-prompt-submit
    55→	}
    56→
    57→	return r.runHookWithInput("user-prompt-submit", input)
    58→}

    60→// SimulateUserPromptSubmitWithResponse simulates the UserPromptSubmit hook
    61→// and returns the parsed hook response (for testing blocking behavior).
    62→func (r *HookRunner) SimulateUserPromptSubmitWithResponse(sessionID string) (*HookResponse, error) {
    63→	r.T.Helper()
    64→
    65→	input := map[string]string{
    66→		"session_id":      sessionID,
    67→		"transcript_path": "", // Not used for user-prompt-submit
    68→	}
    69→
    70→	inputJSON, err := json.Marshal(input)
    71→	if err != nil {
    72→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal hook input: %w", err)
    73→	}
    74→
    75→	output := r.runHookWithOutput("user-prompt-submit", inputJSON)
    76→
    77→	// If hook failed with an error, return the error
    78→	if output.Err != nil {
    79→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("hook failed: %w\nStderr: %s\nStdout: %s",
    80→			output.Err, output.Stderr, output.Stdout)
    81→	}
    82→
    83→	// Parse JSON response from stdout
    84→	var resp HookResponse
    85→	if len(output.Stdout) > 0 {
    86→		if err := json.Unmarshal(output.Stdout, &resp); err != nil {
    87→			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse hook response: %w\nStdout: %s",
    88→				err, output.Stdout)
    89→		}
    90→	}
    91→
    92→	return &resp, nil
    93→}

   180→func (r *HookRunner) runHookInRepoDir(hookName string, inputJSON []byte) error {
   181→	// Run using the shared test binary
   182→	// Command structure: entire hooks claude-code <hook-name>
   183→	cmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "claude-code", hookName)
   184→	cmd.Dir = r.RepoDir
   185→	cmd.Stdin = bytes.NewReader(inputJSON)
   186→	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
   187→		"ENTIRE_TEST_CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="+r.ClaudeProjectDir,
   188→	)
   189→
   190→	output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
   191→	if err != nil {
   192→		return fmt.Errorf("hook %s failed: %w\nInput: %s\nOutput: %s",
   193→			hookName, err, inputJSON, output)
   194→	}
   195→
   196→	r.T.Logf("Hook %s output: %s", hookName, output)
   197→	return nil
   198→}

   200→// Session represents a simulated Claude Code session.
   201→type Session struct {
   202→	ID                string // Raw model session ID (e.g., "test-session-1")
   203→	EntireID          string // Entire session ID with date prefix (e.g., "2025-12-02-test-session-1")
   204→	TranscriptPath    string
   205→	TranscriptBuilder *TranscriptBuilder
   206→	env               *TestEnv
   207→}
   208→
   209→// FileChange represents a file modification in a session.
   210→type FileChange struct {
   211→	Path    string
   212→	Content string
   213→}
   214→
   215→// NewSession creates a new simulated session.
   216→func (env *TestEnv) NewSession() *Session {
   217→	env.T.Helper()
   218→
   219→	env.SessionCounter++
   220→	sessionID := fmt.Sprintf("test-session-%d", env.SessionCounter)
   221→	entireID := sessionid.EntireSessionID(sessionID)
   222→	transcriptPath := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".entire", "tmp", sessionID+".jsonl")
   223→
   224→	return &Session{
   225→		ID:                sessionID,
   226→		EntireID:          entireID,
   227→		TranscriptPath:    transcriptPath,
   228→		TranscriptBuilder: NewTranscriptBuilder(),
   229→		env:               env,
   230→	}
   231→}
   232→
   233→// CreateTranscript builds and writes a transcript for the session.
   234→func (s *Session) CreateTranscript(prompt string, changes []FileChange) string {
   235→	s.TranscriptBuilder.AddUserMessage(prompt)
   236→	s.TranscriptBuilder.AddAssistantMessage("I'll help you with that.")
   237→
   238→	for _, change := range changes {
   239→		toolID := s.TranscriptBuilder.AddToolUse("mcp__acp__Write", change.Path, change.Content)
   240→		s.TranscriptBuilder.AddToolResult(toolID)
   241→	}
   242→
   243→	s.TranscriptBuilder.AddAssistantMessage("Done!")
   244→
   245→	if err := s.TranscriptBuilder.WriteToFile(s.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
   246→		s.env.T.Fatalf("failed to write transcript: %v", err)
   247→	}
   248→
   249→	return s.TranscriptPath
   250→}

   327→// ClearSessionState removes the session state file for the given session ID.
   328→// This simulates what happens when a user commits their changes (session is "completed").
   329→// Used in tests to allow sequential sessions to run without triggering concurrent session warnings.
   330→func (env *TestEnv) ClearSessionState(sessionID string) error {
   331→	env.T.Helper()
   332→
   333→	// Session state is stored in .git/entire-sessions/<session-id>.json
   334→	// Use sessionid.EntireSessionID to get the full session ID with date prefix
   335→	entireSessionID := sessionid.EntireSessionID(sessionID)
   336→	stateFile := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".git", "entire-sessions", entireSessionID+".json")
   337→
   338→	if err := os.Remove(stateFile); err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
   339→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to clear session state: %w", err)
   340→	}
   341→	return nil
   342→}

   344→// HookOutput contains the result of running a hook.
   345→type HookOutput struct {
   346→	Stdout []byte
   347→	Stderr []byte
   348→	Err    error
   349→}
   350→
   351→// runHookWithOutput runs a hook and returns both stdout and stderr separately.
   352→func (r *HookRunner) runHookWithOutput(hookName string, inputJSON []byte) HookOutput {
   353→	cmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "claude-code", hookName)
   354→	cmd.Dir = r.RepoDir
   355→	cmd.Stdin = bytes.NewReader(inputJSON)
   356→	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
   357→		"ENTIRE_TEST_CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="+r.ClaudeProjectDir,
   358→	)
   359→
   360→	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
   361→	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
   362→	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
   363→
   364→	err := cmd.Run()
   365→	return HookOutput{
   366→		Stdout: stdout.Bytes(),
   367→		Stderr: stderr.Bytes(),
   368→		Err:    err,
   369→	}
   370→}

   420→// GetSessionState reads and returns the session state for the given session ID.
   421→func (env *TestEnv) GetSessionState(sessionID string) (*strategy.SessionState, error) {
   422→	env.T.Helper()
   423→
   424→	entireSessionID := sessionid.EntireSessionID(sessionID)
   425→	stateFile := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".git", "entire-sessions", entireSessionID+".json")
   426→
   427→	data, err := os.ReadFile(stateFile)
   428→	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   429→		return nil, nil
   430→	}
   431→	if err != nil {
   432→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read session state: %w", err)
   433→	}
   434→
   435→	var state strategy.SessionState
   436→	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &state); err != nil {
   437→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse session state: %w", err)
   438→	}
   439→	return &state, nil
   440→}

   615→// CreateGeminiTranscript creates a Gemini JSON transcript file for the session.
   616→func (s *GeminiSession) CreateGeminiTranscript(prompt string, changes []FileChange) string {
   617→	// Build Gemini-format transcript (JSON, not JSONL)
   618→	messages := []map[string]interface{}{
   619→		{
   620→			"type":    "user",
   621→			"content": prompt,
   622→		},
   623→		{
   624→			"type":    "assistant",
   625→			"content": "I'll help you with that.",
   626→		},
   627→	}
   628→
   629→	for _, change := range changes {
   630→		messages = append(messages, map[string]interface{}{
   631→			"type": "tool_use",
   632→			"name": "write_file",
   633→			"input": map[string]string{
   634→				"path":    change.Path,
   635→				"content": change.Content,
   636→			},
   637→		})
   638→		messages = append(messages, map[string]interface{}{
   639→			"type":   "tool_result",
   640→			"output": "File written successfully",
   641→		})
   642→	}
   643→
   644→	messages = append(messages, map[string]interface{}{
   645→		"type":    "assistant",
   646→		"content": "Done!",
   647→	})
   648→
   649→	transcript := map[string]interface{}{
   650→		"sessionId": s.ID,
   651→		"messages":  messages,
   652→	}
   653→
   654→	// Ensure directory exists
   655→	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(s.TranscriptPath), 0o755); err != nil {
   656→		s.env.T.Fatalf("failed to create transcript dir: %v", err)
   657→	}
   658→
   659→	// Write transcript
   660→	data, err := json.MarshalIndent(transcript, "", "  ")
   661→	if err != nil {
   662→		s.env.T.Fatalf("failed to marshal transcript: %v", err)
   663→	}
   664→	if err := os.WriteFile(s.TranscriptPath, data, 0o644); err != nil {
   665→		s.env.T.Fatalf("failed to write transcript: %v", err)
   666→	}
   667→
   668→	return s.TranscriptPath
   669→}

    30→// testBinaryPath holds the path to the CLI binary built once in TestMain.
    31→// All tests share this binary to avoid repeated builds.
    32→var testBinaryPath string
    33→
    34→// getTestBinary returns the path to the shared test binary.
    35→// It panics if TestMain hasn't run (testBinaryPath is empty).
    36→func getTestBinary() string {
    37→	if testBinaryPath == "" {
    38→		panic("testBinaryPath not set - TestMain must run before tests")
    39→	}
    40→	return testBinaryPath
    41→}

    43→// TestEnv manages an isolated test environment for integration tests.
    44→type TestEnv struct {
    45→	T                *testing.T
    46→	RepoDir          string
    47→	ClaudeProjectDir string
    48→	GeminiProjectDir string
    49→	SessionCounter   int
    50→}
    51→
    52→// NewTestEnv creates a new isolated test environment.
    53→// It creates temp directories for the git repo and agent project files.
    54→// Note: Does NOT change working directory to allow parallel test execution.
    55→// Note: Does NOT use t.Setenv to allow parallel test execution - CLI commands
    56→// receive the env var via cmd.Env instead.
    57→func NewTestEnv(t *testing.T) *TestEnv {
    58→	t.Helper()
    59→
    60→	// Resolve symlinks on macOS where /var -> /private/var
    61→	// This ensures the CLI subprocess and test use consistent paths
    62→	repoDir := t.TempDir()
    63→	if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(repoDir); err == nil {
    64→		repoDir = resolved
    65→	}
    66→	claudeProjectDir := t.TempDir()
    67→	if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(claudeProjectDir); err == nil {
    68→		claudeProjectDir = resolved
    69→	}
    70→	geminiProjectDir := t.TempDir()
    71→	if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(geminiProjectDir); err == nil {
    72→		geminiProjectDir = resolved
    73→	}
    74→
    75→	env := &TestEnv{
    76→		T:                t,
    77→		RepoDir:          repoDir,
    78→		ClaudeProjectDir: claudeProjectDir,
    79→		GeminiProjectDir: geminiProjectDir,
    80→	}
    81→
    82→	// Note: Don't use t.Setenv here - it's incompatible with t.Parallel()
    83→	// CLI commands receive ENTIRE_TEST_CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR or ENTIRE_TEST_GEMINI_PROJECT_DIR via cmd.Env instead
    84→
    85→	return env
    86→}
    87→
    88→// Cleanup is a no-op retained for backwards compatibility.
    89→//
    90→// Previously this method restored the working directory after NewTestEnv changed it.
    91→// With the refactor to remove os.Chdir from NewTestEnv:
    92→// - Temp directories are now cleaned up automatically by t.TempDir()
    93→// - Working directory is never changed, so no restoration is needed
    94→//
    95→// This method is kept to avoid breaking existing tests that call defer env.Cleanup().
    96→// New tests should not call this method as it serves no purpose.
    97→//
    98→// Deprecated: This method is a no-op and will be removed in a future version.
    99→func (env *TestEnv) Cleanup() {
   100→	// No-op - temp dirs are cleaned up by t.TempDir()
   101→}

   192→// RunForAllStrategies runs a test function for each strategy in parallel.
   193→// This reduces boilerplate for tests that need to verify behavior across all strategies.
   194→// Each subtest gets its own TestEnv with a feature branch ready for testing.
   195→func RunForAllStrategies(t *testing.T, testFn func(t *testing.T, env *TestEnv, strategyName string)) {
   196→	t.Helper()
   197→	for _, strat := range AllStrategies() {
   198→		strat := strat // capture for parallel
   199→		t.Run(strat, func(t *testing.T) {
   200→			t.Parallel()
   201→			env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, strat)
   202→			testFn(t, env, strat)
   203→		})
   204→	}
   205→}
   206→
   207→// RunForAllStrategiesWithRepoEnv runs a test function for each strategy in parallel,
   208→// using NewRepoWithCommit instead of NewFeatureBranchEnv. Use this for tests
   209→// that need to test behavior on the main branch.
   210→func RunForAllStrategiesWithRepoEnv(t *testing.T, testFn func(t *testing.T, env *TestEnv, strategyName string)) {
   211→	t.Helper()
   212→	for _, strat := range AllStrategies() {
   213→		strat := strat // capture for parallel
   214→		t.Run(strat, func(t *testing.T) {
   215→			t.Parallel()
   216→			env := NewRepoWithCommit(t, strat)
   217→			testFn(t, env, strat)
   218→		})
   219→	}
   220→}

   222→// RunForAllStrategiesWithBasicEnv runs a test function for each strategy in parallel,
   223→// using NewRepoEnv (git repo + entire init, no commits). Use this for tests
   224→// that need to verify basic initialization behavior.
   225→func RunForAllStrategiesWithBasicEnv(t *testing.T, testFn func(t *testing.T, env *TestEnv, strategyName string)) {
   226→	t.Helper()
   227→	for _, strat := range AllStrategies() {
   228→		strat := strat // capture for parallel
   229→		t.Run(strat, func(t *testing.T) {
   230→			t.Parallel()
   231→			env := NewRepoEnv(t, strat)
   232→			testFn(t, env, strat)
   233→		})
   234→	}
   235→}

   237→// RunForStrategiesSequential runs a test function for specific strategies sequentially.
   238→// Use this for tests that cannot be parallelized (e.g., tests using os.Chdir).
   239→// The strategies parameter allows testing a subset of strategies.
   240→func RunForStrategiesSequential(t *testing.T, strategies []string, testFn func(t *testing.T, strategyName string)) {
   241→	t.Helper()
   242→	for _, strat := range strategies {
   243→		t.Run(strat, func(t *testing.T) {
   244→			testFn(t, strat)
   245→		})
   246→	}
   247→}

   249→// InitRepo initializes a git repository in the test environment.
   250→func (env *TestEnv) InitRepo() {
   251→	env.T.Helper()
   252→
   253→	repo, err := git.PlainInit(env.RepoDir, false)
   254→	if err != nil {
   255→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to init git repo: %v", err)
   256→	}
   257→
   258→	// Configure git user for commits
   259→	cfg, err := repo.Config()
   260→	if err != nil {
   261→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to get repo config: %v", err)
   262→	}
   263→	cfg.User.Name = "Test User"
   264→	cfg.User.Email = "test@example.com"
   265→
   266→	// Disable GPG signing for test commits (prevents failures if user has commit.gpgsign=true globally)
   267→	if cfg.Raw == nil {
   268→		cfg.Raw = config.New()
   269→	}
   270→	cfg.Raw.Section("commit").SetOption("gpgsign", "false")
   271→
   272→	if err := repo.SetConfig(cfg); err != nil {
   273→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to set repo config: %v", err)
   274→	}
   275→}

   301→// initEntireInternal is the common implementation for InitEntire variants.
   302→func (env *TestEnv) initEntireInternal(strategyName string, agentName agent.AgentName, strategyOptions map[string]any) {
   303→	env.T.Helper()
   304→
   305→	// Create .entire directory structure
   306→	entireDir := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".entire")
   307→	if err := os.MkdirAll(entireDir, 0o755); err != nil {
   308→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to create .entire directory: %v", err)
   309→	}
   310→
   311→	// Create tmp directory
   312→	tmpDir := filepath.Join(entireDir, "tmp")
   313→	if err := os.MkdirAll(tmpDir, 0o755); err != nil {
   314→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to create .entire/tmp directory: %v", err)
   315→	}
   316→
   317→	// Write settings.json
   318→	settings := map[string]any{
   319→		"strategy":  strategyName,
   320→		"local_dev": true, // Use go run for hooks in tests
   321→	}
   322→	// Only add agent if specified (otherwise defaults to claude-code)
   323→	if agentName != "" {
   324→		settings["agent"] = string(agentName)
   325→	}
   326→	if strategyOptions != nil {
   327→		settings["strategy_options"] = strategyOptions
   328→	}
   329→	data, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(settings, "", "  ")
   330→	if err != nil {
   331→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to marshal settings: %v", err)
   332→	}
   333→	settingsPath := filepath.Join(entireDir, paths.SettingsFileName)
   334→	if err := os.WriteFile(settingsPath, data, 0o644); err != nil {
   335→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to write %s: %v", paths.SettingsFileName, err)
   336→	}
   337→}

   638→// RewindPoint mirrors strategy.RewindPoint for test assertions.
   639→type RewindPoint struct {
   640→	ID               string
   641→	Message          string
   642→	MetadataDir      string
   643→	Date             time.Time
   644→	IsTaskCheckpoint bool
   645→	ToolUseID        string
   646→	IsLogsOnly       bool

   650→// GetRewindPoints returns available rewind points using the CLI.
   651→func (env *TestEnv) GetRewindPoints() []RewindPoint {
   652→	env.T.Helper()
   653→
   654→	// Run rewind --list using the shared binary
   655→	cmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "rewind", "--list")
   656→	cmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
   657→	cmd.Env = env.cliEnv()
   658→
   659→	output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
   660→	if err != nil {
   661→		env.T.Fatalf("rewind --list failed: %v\nOutput: %s", err, output)
   662→	}
   663→
   664→	// Parse JSON output
   665→	var jsonPoints []struct {
   666→		ID               string `json:"id"`
   667→		Message          string `json:"message"`
   668→		MetadataDir      string `json:"metadata_dir"`
   669→		Date             string `json:"date"`
   670→		IsTaskCheckpoint bool   `json:"is_task_checkpoint"`
   671→		ToolUseID        string `json:"tool_use_id"`
   672→		IsLogsOnly       bool   `json:"is_logs_only"`
   673→		CondensationID   string `json:"condensation_id"`
   674→	}
   675→
   676→	if err := json.Unmarshal(output, &jsonPoints); err != nil {
   677→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to parse rewind points: %v\nOutput: %s", err, output)
   678→	}
   679→
   680→	points := make([]RewindPoint, len(jsonPoints))
   681→	for i, jp := range jsonPoints {
   682→		date, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, jp.Date)
   683→		points[i] = RewindPoint{
   684→			ID:               jp.ID,
   685→			Message:          jp.Message,
   686→			MetadataDir:      jp.MetadataDir,
   687→			Date:             date,
   688→			IsTaskCheckpoint: jp.IsTaskCheckpoint,
   689→			ToolUseID:        jp.ToolUseID,
   690→			IsLogsOnly:       jp.IsLogsOnly,
   691→			CondensationID:   jp.CondensationID,
   692→		}
   693→	}
   694→
   695→	return points
   696→}

   797→// FileExistsInBranch checks if a file exists in a specific branch's tree.
   798→func (env *TestEnv) FileExistsInBranch(branchName, filePath string) bool {
   799→	env.T.Helper()
   800→
   801→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
   802→	if err != nil {
   803→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)
   804→	}
   805→
   806→	// Get the branch reference
   807→	ref, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(branchName), true)
   808→	if err != nil {
   809→		// Try as a remote-style ref
   810→		ref, err = repo.Reference(plumbing.ReferenceName("refs/heads/"+branchName), true)
   811→		if err != nil {
   812→			return false
   813→		}
   814→	}
   815→
   816→	// Get the commit
   817→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   818→	if err != nil {
   819→		return false
   820→	}
   821→
   822→	// Get the tree
   823→	tree, err := commit.Tree()
   824→	if err != nil {
   825→		return false
   826→	}
   827→
   828→	// Check if file exists
   829→	_, err = tree.File(filePath)
   830→	return err == nil
   831→}

   844→	ref, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(branchName), true)
   845→	if err != nil {
   846→		// Try as a remote-style ref
   847→		ref, err = repo.Reference(plumbing.ReferenceName("refs/heads/"+branchName), true)
   848→		if err != nil {
   849→			return "", false
   850→		}
   851→	}
   852→
   853→	// Get the commit
   854→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   855→	if err != nil {
   856→		return "", false
   857→	}
   858→
   859→	// Get the tree

   865→	// Get the file

   904→// GitCommitWithShadowHooks stages and commits files, simulating the prepare-commit-msg
   905→// and post-commit hooks as a human (with TTY). This is the default for tests.
   906→func (env *TestEnv) GitCommitWithShadowHooks(message string, files ...string) {
   907→	env.T.Helper()
   908→	env.gitCommitWithShadowHooks(message, true, files...)
   909→}
   910→
   911→// GitCommitWithShadowHooksAsAgent is like GitCommitWithShadowHooks but simulates
   912→// an agent commit (no TTY). This triggers the fast path in PrepareCommitMsg that
   913→// skips content detection and interactive prompts for ACTIVE sessions.
   914→func (env *TestEnv) GitCommitWithShadowHooksAsAgent(message string, files ...string) {
   915→	env.T.Helper()
   916→	env.gitCommitWithShadowHooks(message, false, files...)
   917→}
   918→
   919→// gitCommitWithShadowHooks is the shared implementation for committing with shadow hooks.
   920→// When simulateTTY is true, sets ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1 to simulate a human at the terminal.
   921→// When false, filters it out to simulate an agent subprocess (no controlling terminal).
   922→func (env *TestEnv) gitCommitWithShadowHooks(message string, simulateTTY bool, files ...string) {
   923→	env.T.Helper()
   924→
   925→	// Stage files using go-git
   926→	for _, file := range files {
   927→		env.GitAdd(file)
   928→	}
   929→
   930→	// Create a temp file for the commit message (prepare-commit-msg hook modifies this)
   931→	msgFile := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".git", "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
   932→	if err := os.WriteFile(msgFile, []byte(message), 0o644); err != nil {
   933→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to write commit message file: %v", err)
   934→	}
   935→
   936→	// Run prepare-commit-msg hook using the shared binary.
   937→	// Pass source="message" to match real `git commit -m` behavior.
   938→	prepCmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "git", "prepare-commit-msg", msgFile, "message")
   939→	prepCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
   940→	if simulateTTY {
   941→		// Simulate human at terminal: ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1 makes hasTTY() return true
   942→		// and askConfirmTTY() return defaultYes without reading from /dev/tty.
   943→		prepCmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1")
   944→	} else {
   945→		// Simulate agent: ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0 makes hasTTY() return false,
   946→		// triggering the fast path that adds trailers for ACTIVE sessions.
   947→		prepCmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0")
   948→	}
   949→	if output, err := prepCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
   950→		env.T.Logf("prepare-commit-msg output: %s", output)
   951→		// Don't fail - hook may silently succeed
   952→	}
   953→
   954→	// Read the modified message
   955→	modifiedMsg, err := os.ReadFile(msgFile)
   956→	if err != nil {
   957→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to read modified commit message: %v", err)
   958→	}
   959→
   960→	// Create the commit using go-git with the modified message
   961→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
   962→	if err != nil {
   963→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)
   964→	}
   965→
   966→	worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
   967→	if err != nil {
   968→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to get worktree: %v", err)
   969→	}
   970→
   971→	_, err = worktree.Commit(string(modifiedMsg), &git.CommitOptions{
   972→		Author: &object.Signature{
   973→			Name:  "Test User",
   974→			Email: "test@example.com",
   975→			When:  time.Now(),
   976→		},
   977→	})
   978→	if err != nil {
   979→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to commit: %v", err)
   980→	}
   981→
   982→	// Run post-commit hook using the shared binary
   983→	// This triggers condensation if the commit has an Entire-Checkpoint trailer
   984→	postCmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "git", "post-commit")
   985→	postCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
   986→	if output, err := postCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
   987→		env.T.Logf("post-commit output: %s", output)
   988→		// Don't fail - hook may silently succeed
   989→	}
   990→}
   991→
   992→// GitCommitAmendWithShadowHooks amends the last commit with shadow hooks.
   993→// This simulates `git commit --amend` with the prepare-commit-msg and post-commit hooks.
   994→// The prepare-commit-msg hook is called with "commit" source to indicate an amend.
   995→func (env *TestEnv) GitCommitAmendWithShadowHooks(message string, files ...string) {
   996→	env.T.Helper()
   997→
   998→	// Stage any additional files
   999→	for _, file := range files {
  1000→		env.GitAdd(file)
  1001→	}
  1002→
  1003→	// Write commit message to temp file
  1004→	msgFile := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".git", "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
  1005→	if err := os.WriteFile(msgFile, []byte(message), 0o644); err != nil {
  1006→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to write commit message file: %v", err)
  1007→	}
  1008→
  1009→	// Run prepare-commit-msg hook with "commit" source (indicates amend).
  1010→	// Set ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1 to simulate human (amend is always a human operation).
  1011→	prepCmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "git", "prepare-commit-msg", msgFile, "commit")
  1012→	prepCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
  1013→	prepCmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1")
  1014→	if output, err := prepCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
  1015→		env.T.Logf("prepare-commit-msg (amend) output: %s", output)
  1016→	}
  1017→
  1018→	// Read the modified message
  1019→	modifiedMsg, err := os.ReadFile(msgFile)
  1020→	if err != nil {
  1021→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to read modified commit message: %v", err)
  1022→	}
  1023→
  1024→	// Amend the commit using go-git
  1025→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
  1026→	if err != nil {
  1027→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)

  1055→// GitCommitWithTrailerRemoved stages and commits files, simulating what happens when
  1056→// a user removes the Entire-Checkpoint trailer during commit message editing.
  1057→// This tests the opt-out behavior where removing the trailer skips condensation.
  1058→func (env *TestEnv) GitCommitWithTrailerRemoved(message string, files ...string) {
  1059→	env.T.Helper()
  1060→
  1061→	// Stage files using go-git
  1062→	for _, file := range files {
  1063→		env.GitAdd(file)
  1064→	}
  1065→
  1066→	// Create a temp file for the commit message (prepare-commit-msg hook modifies this)
  1067→	msgFile := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".git", "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
  1068→	if err := os.WriteFile(msgFile, []byte(message), 0o644); err != nil {
  1069→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to write commit message file: %v", err)
  1070→	}
  1071→
  1072→	// Run prepare-commit-msg hook using the shared binary.
  1073→	// Set ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1 to simulate human (this tests the editor flow where
  1074→	// the user removes the trailer before committing).
  1075→	prepCmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "git", "prepare-commit-msg", msgFile)
  1076→	prepCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
  1077→	prepCmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1")
  1078→	if output, err := prepCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
  1079→		env.T.Logf("prepare-commit-msg output: %s", output)
  1080→	}
  1081→
  1082→	// Read the modified message (with trailer added by hook)
  1083→	modifiedMsg, err := os.ReadFile(msgFile)
  1084→	if err != nil {
  1085→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to read modified commit message: %v", err)
  1086→	}
  1087→
  1088→	// REMOVE the Entire-Checkpoint trailer (simulating user editing the message)
  1089→	lines := strings.Split(string(modifiedMsg), "\n")
  1090→	var cleanedLines []string
  1091→	for _, line := range lines {
  1092→		// Skip the trailer and the comments about it
  1093→		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "Entire-Checkpoint:") {
  1094→			continue
  1095→		}
  1096→		if strings.Contains(line, "Remove the Entire-Checkpoint trailer") {
  1097→			continue
  1098→		}
  1099→		if strings.Contains(line, "trailer will be added to your next commit") {
  1100→			continue
  1101→		}
  1102→		cleanedLines = append(cleanedLines, line)
  1103→	}
  1104→	cleanedMsg := strings.TrimRight(strings.Join(cleanedLines, "\n"), "\n") + "\n"
  1105→
  1106→	// Create the commit using go-git with the cleaned message (no trailer)
  1107→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
  1108→	if err != nil {
  1109→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)
  1110→	}
  1111→
  1112→	worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
  1113→	if err != nil {
  1114→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to get worktree: %v", err)
  1115→	}
  1116→
  1117→	_, err = worktree.Commit(cleanedMsg, &git.CommitOptions{
  1118→		Author: &object.Signature{
  1119→			Name:  "Test User",
  1120→			Email: "test@example.com",
  1121→			When:  time.Now(),
  1122→		},
  1123→	})
  1124→	if err != nil {
  1125→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to commit: %v", err)
  1126→	}
  1127→
  1128→	// Run post-commit hook - since trailer was removed, no condensation should happen
  1129→	postCmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "git", "post-commit")
  1130→	postCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
  1131→	if output, err := postCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
  1132→		env.T.Logf("post-commit output: %s", output)
  1133→	}
  1134→}

  1162→// GetLatestCheckpointID returns the most recent checkpoint ID from the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch.
  1163→// This is used by tests that previously extracted the checkpoint ID from commit message trailers.
  1164→// Now that active branch commits are clean (no trailers), we get the ID from the sessions branch.

  1166→func (env *TestEnv) GetLatestCheckpointID() string {
  1167→	env.T.Helper()
  1168→
  1169→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
  1170→	if err != nil {
  1171→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)

  1173→
  1174→	// Get the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch

  1188→	for _, line := range strings.Split(commit.Message, "\n") {
  1189→		line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
  1190→		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "Checkpoint: ") {
  1191→			return strings.TrimPrefix(line, "Checkpoint: ")

  1193→	}
  1194→
  1195→	env.T.Fatalf("could not find checkpoint ID in %s branch commit message:\n%s",
  1196→		paths.MetadataBranchName, commit.Message)

  1198→}

  1253→// GetLatestCheckpointIDFromHistory walks backwards from HEAD on the active branch
  1254→// and returns the checkpoint ID from the first commit that has an Entire-Checkpoint trailer.
  1255→// This verifies that condensation actually happened (commit has trailer) without relying
  1256→// on timestamp-based matching.
  1257→func (env *TestEnv) GetLatestCheckpointIDFromHistory() string {
  1258→	env.T.Helper()
  1259→
  1260→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
  1261→	if err != nil {
  1262→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)
  1263→	}
  1264→
  1265→	head, err := repo.Head()
  1266→	if err != nil {
  1267→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to get HEAD: %v", err)
  1268→	}
  1269→
  1270→	commitIter, err := repo.Log(&git.LogOptions{From: head.Hash()})
  1271→	if err != nil {
  1272→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to iterate commits: %v", err)
  1273→	}
  1274→
  1275→	var checkpointID string
  1276→	//nolint:errcheck // ForEach callback handles errors
  1277→	commitIter.ForEach(func(c *object.Commit) error {
  1278→		if cpID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(c.Message); found {
  1279→			checkpointID = cpID.String()
  1280→			return errors.New("stop iteration") // Found it, stop
  1281→		}
  1282→		return nil
  1283→	})
  1284→
  1285→	if checkpointID == "" {
  1286→		env.T.Fatalf("no commit with Entire-Checkpoint trailer found in history")
  1287→	}
  1288→
  1289→	return checkpointID
  1290→}

  1316→func findModuleRoot() string {
  1317→	// Start from this source file's location and walk up to find go.mod
  1318→	_, thisFile, _, ok := runtime.Caller(0)
  1319→	if !ok {
  1320→		panic("failed to get current file path via runtime.Caller")
  1321→	}
  1322→	dir := filepath.Dir(thisFile)
  1323→
  1324→	for {
  1325→		if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, "go.mod")); err == nil {
  1326→			return dir
  1327→		}
  1328→		parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
  1329→		if parent == dir {
  1330→			panic("could not find go.mod starting from " + thisFile)
  1331→		}
  1332→		dir = parent
  1333→	}
  1334→}

   153→// WriteToFile writes the transcript to a JSONL file.
   154→func (b *TranscriptBuilder) WriteToFile(path string) error {
   155→	// Ensure directory exists
   156→	dir := filepath.Dir(path)
   157→	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
   158→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create directory: %w", err)
   159→	}
   160→
   161→	file, err := os.Create(path)
   162→	if err != nil {
   163→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create file: %w", err)
   164→	}
   165→	defer func() { _ = file.Close() }()
   166→
   167→	encoder := json.NewEncoder(file)
   168→	for _, msg := range b.messages {
   169→		if err := encoder.Encode(msg); err != nil {
   170→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to encode message: %w", err)
   171→		}
   172→	}
   173→	return nil
   174→}

   176→// String returns the transcript as a JSONL string.
   177→func (b *TranscriptBuilder) String() string {
   178→	var result string
   179→	var resultSb176 strings.Builder
   180→	for _, msg := range b.messages {
   181→		data, _ := json.Marshal(msg)
   182→		resultSb176.WriteString(string(data) + "\n")
   183→	}
   184→	result += resultSb176.String()
   185→	return result
   186→}

    36→func hasTTY() bool {

    48→// askConfirmTTY prompts the user for a yes/no confirmation via /dev/tty.

    50→// Returns true for yes, false for no. If TTY is unavailable, returns the default.
    51→// If context is non-empty, it is displayed on a separate line before the prompt.
    52→func askConfirmTTY(prompt string, context string, defaultYes bool) bool {
    53→	// In test mode, don't try to interact with the real TTY — just use the default.

    59→
    60→	// Open /dev/tty for both reading and writing

   102→
   103→// CommitMsg is called by the git commit-msg hook after the user edits the message.
   104→// If the message contains only our trailer (no actual user content), strip it
   105→// so git will abort the commit due to empty message.
   106→//
   107→//nolint:unparam // error return required by interface but hooks must return nil
   108→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) CommitMsg(commitMsgFile string) error {
   109→	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile) //nolint:gosec // Path comes from git hook
   110→	if err != nil {
   111→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   112→	}
   113→
   114→	message := string(content)
   115→
   116→	// Check if our trailer is present (ParseCheckpoint validates format, so found==true means valid)
   117→	if _, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(message); !found {
   118→		// No trailer, nothing to do
   119→		return nil
   120→	}
   121→
   122→	// Check if there's any user content (non-comment, non-trailer lines)
   123→	if !hasUserContent(message) {
   124→		// No user content - strip the trailer so git aborts
   125→		message = stripCheckpointTrailer(message)
   126→		if err := os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(message), 0o600); err != nil {
   127→			return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   128→		}
   129→	}
   130→
   131→	return nil
   132→}
   133→
   134→// hasUserContent checks if the message has any content besides comments and our trailer.
   135→func hasUserContent(message string) bool {
   136→	trailerPrefix := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ":"
   137→	for _, line := range strings.Split(message, "\n") {
   138→		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
   139→		// Skip empty lines
   140→		if trimmed == "" {
   141→			continue
   142→		}
   143→		// Skip comment lines
   144→		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "#") {
   145→			continue
   146→		}
   147→		// Skip our trailer line
   148→		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, trailerPrefix) {
   149→			continue
   150→		}
   151→		// Found user content
   152→		return true
   153→	}
   154→	return false
   155→}
   156→
   157→// stripCheckpointTrailer removes the Entire-Checkpoint trailer line from the message.
   158→func stripCheckpointTrailer(message string) string {
   159→	trailerPrefix := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ":"
   160→	var result []string
   161→	for _, line := range strings.Split(message, "\n") {
   162→		if !strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(line), trailerPrefix) {
   163→			result = append(result, line)
   164→		}
   165→	}
   166→	return strings.Join(result, "\n")
   167→}
   168→
   169→// isGitSequenceOperation checks if git is currently in the middle of a rebase,
   170→// cherry-pick, or revert operation. During these operations, commits are being
   171→// replayed and should not be linked to agent sessions.
   172→//
   173→// Detects:
   174→//   - rebase: .git/rebase-merge/ or .git/rebase-apply/ directories
   175→//   - cherry-pick: .git/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD file
   176→//   - revert: .git/REVERT_HEAD file
   177→func isGitSequenceOperation() bool {
   178→	// Get git directory (handles worktrees and relative paths correctly)
   179→	gitDir, err := GetGitDir()
   180→	if err != nil {
   181→		return false // Can't determine, assume not in sequence operation
   182→	}
   183→
   184→	// Check for rebase state directories
   185→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "rebase-merge")); err == nil {
   186→		return true
   187→	}
   188→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "rebase-apply")); err == nil {
   189→		return true
   190→	}
   191→
   192→	// Check for cherry-pick and revert state files
   193→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "CHERRY_PICK_HEAD")); err == nil {
   194→		return true
   195→	}
   196→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "REVERT_HEAD")); err == nil {
   197→		return true
   198→	}
   199→
   200→	return false

   453→// PostCommit is called by the git post-commit hook after a commit is created.
   454→// Uses the session state machine to determine what action to take per session:
   455→//   - ACTIVE → condense immediately (each commit gets its own checkpoint)
   456→//   - IDLE → condense immediately
   457→//   - ENDED → condense if files touched, discard if empty
   458→//
   459→// After condensation for ACTIVE sessions, remaining uncommitted files are
   460→// carried forward to a new shadow branch so the next commit gets its own checkpoint.
   461→//
   462→// Shadow branches are only deleted when ALL sessions sharing the branch are non-active
   463→// and were condensed during this PostCommit.
   464→// During rebase/cherry-pick/revert operations, phase transitions are skipped entirely.
   465→//
   466→//nolint:unparam // error return required by interface but hooks must return nil
   467→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) PostCommit() error {

    10→
    11→// Phase represents the lifecycle stage of a session.
    12→type Phase string
    13→
    14→const (
    15→	PhaseActive Phase = "active"
    16→	PhaseIdle   Phase = "idle"
    17→	PhaseEnded  Phase = "ended"
    18→)
    19→
    20→// allPhases is the canonical list of phases for enumeration (e.g., diagram generation).
    21→var allPhases = []Phase{PhaseIdle, PhaseActive, PhaseEnded}
    22→
    23→// PhaseFromString normalizes a phase string, treating empty or unknown values
    24→// as PhaseIdle for backward compatibility with pre-state-machine session files.
    25→func PhaseFromString(s string) Phase {
    26→	switch Phase(s) {
    27→	case PhaseActive, "active_committed":
    28→		// "active_committed" was removed but meant "agent active + commit happened".
    29→		// Normalize to ACTIVE so HandleTurnEnd can finalize any pending checkpoints.
    30→		return PhaseActive
    31→	case PhaseIdle:
    32→		return PhaseIdle
    33→	case PhaseEnded:
    34→		return PhaseEnded
    35→	default:
    36→		// Backward compat: truly unknown phases normalize to idle.
    37→		return PhaseIdle
    38→	}
    39→}
    40→
    41→// IsActive reports whether the phase represents an active agent turn.
    42→func (p Phase) IsActive() bool {
    43→	return p == PhaseActive
    44→}
    45→
    46→// Event represents something that happened to a session.
    47→type Event int
    48→
    49→const (
    50→	EventTurnStart    Event = iota // Agent begins working on a prompt
    51→	EventTurnEnd                   // Agent finishes its turn
    52→	EventGitCommit                 // A git commit was made (PostCommit hook)
    53→	EventSessionStart              // Session process started (SessionStart hook)
    54→	EventSessionStop               // Session process ended (SessionStop hook)
    55→)
    56→
    57→// allEvents is the canonical list of events for enumeration.
    58→var allEvents = []Event{EventTurnStart, EventTurnEnd, EventGitCommit, EventSessionStart, EventSessionStop}
    59→
    60→// String returns a human-readable name for the event.
    61→func (e Event) String() string {
    62→	switch e {
    63→	case EventTurnStart:
    64→		return "TurnStart"
    65→	case EventTurnEnd:
    66→		return "TurnEnd"
    67→	case EventGitCommit:
    68→		return "GitCommit"
    69→	case EventSessionStart:
    70→		return "SessionStart"
    71→	case EventSessionStop:
    72→		return "SessionStop"
    73→	default:
    74→		return fmt.Sprintf("Event(%d)", int(e))
    75→	}
    76→}
    77→
    78→// Action represents a side effect that should be performed after a transition.
    79→// The caller is responsible for executing these -- the state machine only declares them.
    80→type Action int
    81→
    82→const (
    83→	ActionCondense               Action = iota // Condense session data to permanent storage
    84→	ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched               // Condense only if FilesTouched is non-empty
    85→	ActionDiscardIfNoFiles                     // Discard session if FilesTouched is empty
    86→	ActionWarnStaleSession                     // Warn user about stale session(s)
    87→	ActionClearEndedAt                         // Clear EndedAt timestamp (session re-entering)
    88→	ActionUpdateLastInteraction                // Update LastInteractionTime
    89→)

    91→// String returns a human-readable name for the action.
    92→func (a Action) String() string {

    96→	case ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched:
    97→		return "CondenseIfFilesTouched"
    98→	case ActionDiscardIfNoFiles:
    99→		return "DiscardIfNoFiles"
   100→	case ActionWarnStaleSession:
   101→		return "WarnStaleSession"
   102→	case ActionClearEndedAt:
   103→		return "ClearEndedAt"
   104→	case ActionUpdateLastInteraction:
   105→		return "UpdateLastInteraction"
   106→	default:

   108→	}

   110→
   111→// TransitionContext provides read-only context for transitions that need
   112→// to inspect session state without mutating it.
   113→type TransitionContext struct {
   114→	HasFilesTouched    bool // len(FilesTouched) > 0
   115→	IsRebaseInProgress bool // .git/rebase-merge/ or .git/rebase-apply/ exists
   116→}
   117→
   118→// TransitionResult holds the outcome of a state machine transition.
   119→type TransitionResult struct {
   120→	NewPhase Phase
   121→	Actions  []Action
   122→}
   123→
   124→// Transition computes the next phase and required actions given the current
   125→// phase and an event. This is a pure function with no side effects.
   126→//
   127→// Empty or unknown phase values are normalized to PhaseIdle for backward
   128→// compatibility with session state files created before phase tracking.
   129→func Transition(current Phase, event Event, ctx TransitionContext) TransitionResult {
   130→	// Normalize empty/unknown phase to idle for backward compatibility.
   131→	current = PhaseFromString(string(current))
   132→
   133→	switch current {
   134→	case PhaseIdle:
   135→		return transitionFromIdle(event, ctx)
   136→	case PhaseActive:
   137→		return transitionFromActive(event, ctx)
   138→	case PhaseEnded:
   139→		return transitionFromEnded(event, ctx)
   140→	default:
   141→		// PhaseFromString guarantees we only get known phases, but the
   142→		// exhaustive linter requires handling the default case.
   143→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseIdle}
   144→	}
   145→}
   146→
   147→func transitionFromIdle(event Event, ctx TransitionContext) TransitionResult {
   148→	switch event {
   149→	case EventTurnStart:
   150→		return TransitionResult{
   151→			NewPhase: PhaseActive,
   152→			Actions:  []Action{ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   153→		}
   154→	case EventTurnEnd:
   155→		// Turn end while idle is a no-op (no active turn to end).
   156→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseIdle}
   157→	case EventGitCommit:
   158→		if ctx.IsRebaseInProgress {
   159→			return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseIdle}
   160→		}
   161→		return TransitionResult{
   162→			NewPhase: PhaseIdle,
   163→			Actions:  []Action{ActionCondense, ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   164→		}
   165→	case EventSessionStart:
   166→		// Already condensable, no-op.
   167→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseIdle}
   168→	case EventSessionStop:
   169→		return TransitionResult{
   170→			NewPhase: PhaseEnded,
   171→			Actions:  []Action{ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   172→		}
   173→	default:
   174→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseIdle}
   175→	}
   176→}
   177→
   178→func transitionFromActive(event Event, ctx TransitionContext) TransitionResult {
   179→	switch event {
   180→	case EventTurnStart:
   181→		// Ctrl-C recovery: agent crashed or user interrupted mid-turn.
   182→		return TransitionResult{
   183→			NewPhase: PhaseActive,
   184→			Actions:  []Action{ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   185→		}
   186→	case EventTurnEnd:
   187→		return TransitionResult{
   188→			NewPhase: PhaseIdle,
   189→			Actions:  []Action{ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   190→		}
   191→	case EventGitCommit:
   192→		if ctx.IsRebaseInProgress {
   193→			return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseActive}
   194→		}
   195→		return TransitionResult{
   196→			NewPhase: PhaseActive,
   197→			Actions:  []Action{ActionCondense, ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   198→		}
   199→	case EventSessionStart:
   200→		return TransitionResult{
   201→			NewPhase: PhaseActive,
   202→			Actions:  []Action{ActionWarnStaleSession},
   203→		}
   204→	case EventSessionStop:
   205→		return TransitionResult{
   206→			NewPhase: PhaseEnded,
   207→			Actions:  []Action{ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   208→		}
   209→	default:
   210→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseActive}
   211→	}
   212→}
   213→
   214→func transitionFromEnded(event Event, ctx TransitionContext) TransitionResult {
   215→	switch event {
   216→	case EventTurnStart:
   217→		return TransitionResult{
   218→			NewPhase: PhaseActive,
   219→			Actions:  []Action{ActionClearEndedAt, ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   220→		}
   221→	case EventTurnEnd:
   222→		// Turn end while ended is a no-op.
   223→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseEnded}
   224→	case EventGitCommit:
   225→		if ctx.IsRebaseInProgress {
   226→			return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseEnded}
   227→		}
   228→		if ctx.HasFilesTouched {
   229→			return TransitionResult{
   230→				NewPhase: PhaseEnded,
   231→				Actions:  []Action{ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched, ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   232→			}
   233→		}
   234→		return TransitionResult{
   235→			NewPhase: PhaseEnded,
   236→			Actions:  []Action{ActionDiscardIfNoFiles, ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
   237→		}
   238→	case EventSessionStart:
   239→		return TransitionResult{
   240→			NewPhase: PhaseIdle,
   241→			Actions:  []Action{ActionClearEndedAt},
   242→		}
   243→	case EventSessionStop:
   244→		// Already ended, no-op.
   245→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseEnded}
   246→	default:
   247→		return TransitionResult{NewPhase: PhaseEnded}
   248→	}
   249→}
   250→
   251→// ApplyCommonActions applies the common (non-strategy-specific) actions from a
   252→// TransitionResult to the given State. It updates Phase, LastInteractionTime,
   253→// and EndedAt as indicated by the transition.
   254→//
   255→// Returns the subset of actions that require strategy-specific handling
   256→// (e.g., ActionCondense, ActionWarnStaleSession).
   257→// The caller is responsible for dispatching those.
   258→func ApplyCommonActions(state *State, result TransitionResult) []Action {
   259→	state.Phase = result.NewPhase
   260→
   261→	var remaining []Action
   262→	for _, action := range result.Actions {
   263→		switch action {
   264→		case ActionUpdateLastInteraction:
   265→			now := time.Now()
   266→			state.LastInteractionTime = &now
   267→		case ActionClearEndedAt:
   268→			state.EndedAt = nil
   269→		case ActionCondense, ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched, ActionDiscardIfNoFiles,
   270→			ActionWarnStaleSession:
   271→			// Strategy-specific actions — pass through to caller.
   272→			remaining = append(remaining, action)
   273→		}
   274→	}
   275→	return remaining
   276→}
   277→
   278→// MermaidDiagram generates a Mermaid state diagram from the transition table.
   279→// The diagram is derived by calling Transition() for representative context
   280→// variants per phase/event, so it stays in sync with the implementation.
   281→func MermaidDiagram() string {
   282→	var b strings.Builder
   283→	b.WriteString("stateDiagram-v2\n")
   284→
   285→	// State declarations with descriptions.
   286→	b.WriteString("    state \"IDLE\" as idle\n")
   287→	b.WriteString("    state \"ACTIVE\" as active\n")
   288→	b.WriteString("    state \"ENDED\" as ended\n")
   289→	b.WriteString("\n")
   290→
   291→	// Context variants for GitCommit: rebase, files/no-files.
   292→	type contextVariant struct {
   293→		label string
   294→		ctx   TransitionContext
   295→	}
   296→
   297→	// For each phase/event, generate edges.
   298→	for _, phase := range allPhases {
   299→		for _, event := range allEvents {
   300→			var variants []contextVariant
   301→			switch {
   302→			case event == EventGitCommit && phase == PhaseEnded:
   303→				// HasFilesTouched only affects PhaseEnded transitions;
   304→				// other phases produce identical edges for both values.
   305→				variants = []contextVariant{
   306→					{"[files]", TransitionContext{HasFilesTouched: true}},
   307→					{"[no files]", TransitionContext{HasFilesTouched: false}},
   308→					{"[rebase]", TransitionContext{IsRebaseInProgress: true}},
   309→				}
   310→			case event == EventGitCommit:
   311→				variants = []contextVariant{
   312→					{"", TransitionContext{}},
   313→					{"[rebase]", TransitionContext{IsRebaseInProgress: true}},
   314→				}
   315→			default:
   316→				variants = []contextVariant{
   317→					{"", TransitionContext{}},
   318→				}
   319→			}
   320→
   321→			for _, v := range variants {
   322→				result := Transition(phase, event, v.ctx)
   323→
   324→				// Build edge label.
   325→				label := event.String()
   326→				if v.label != "" {
   327→					label += " " + v.label
   328→				}
   329→				if len(result.Actions) > 0 {
   330→					actionNames := make([]string, 0, len(result.Actions))
   331→					for _, a := range result.Actions {
   332→						actionNames = append(actionNames, a.String())
   333→					}
   334→					label += " / " + strings.Join(actionNames, ", ")
   335→				}
   336→
   337→				from := string(phase)
   338→				to := string(result.NewPhase)
   339→
   340→				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "    %s --> %s : %s\n", from, to, label)
   341→			}
   342→		}
   343→	}
   344→
   345→	return b.String()
   346→}
   347→

   197→		t.Fatalf("SimulateUserPromptSubmit failed: %v", err)
   198→	}
   199→
   200→	// Create a file and commit as agent (no TTY)
   201→	env.WriteFile("agent_file.txt", "created by agent")
   202→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooksAsAgent("Agent commit", "agent_file.txt")
   203→
   204→	// Agent commits should ALWAYS get a trailer (fast path, no content detection)
   205→	commitHash := env.GetHeadHash()
   206→	checkpointID := env.GetCheckpointIDFromCommitMessage(commitHash)
   207→	if checkpointID == "" {
   208→		t.Error("Agent commit during ACTIVE session should always get a checkpoint trailer")
   209→	} else {
   210→		t.Logf("Agent commit correctly got checkpoint trailer: %s", checkpointID)
   211→	}
   212→}
